articleTitle: Using the ESP32 Microcontroller for Data Processing
abstract: This article deals with experiences with the development of applications of the ESP32 microcontrollers and provides a comprehensive review of the possibilities of applications development on this platform in the area of data measurement and processing. Microcontrollers usually connect with IoT modules and other smart sensors and provide data to the superior system. This paper also describes implementation of application with the version of connected OLED display and with ESP32 Wrover development board with integrated display.

articleTitle: Virtualization of Production Using Digital Twin Technology
abstract: The contribution deals with current situation in modern manufacturing enterprises, which is affected by digital virtualization of different parts of the production process. The overview part of this article points to the fact, that wide informatization of all areas causes substitution of real elements and relationships between them with their digital, often virtual images, in real practice. Key characteristics of the systems implemented using digital twin technology along with essential conditions for intelligent products deployment were identified across many published studies. The goal is to outline an option for the production system realization using digital twin technology as a supplement of standardized concepts for Industry 4.0. The main resulting idea leads to the statement that the current trend of implementation of the new technologies and ways of communication between industrial facilities erases the boundaries between the real environment and the virtual world. The final part of the paper is devoted to implementing the proposed concept using the AVEVA Wonderware software tool.

articleTitle: A Review of the Virtual Reality Applications in Education and Training
abstract: Virtual reality technologies for supporting teaching and learning have been an academic research topic for decades. In the last five years, major progress have been made and the virtual reality technology is getting closer to being implemented in education. This paper presents an overview of the uses of virtual reality in education, specifically on the Oculus Rift platform. The purpose of this study is to explore the current use of virtual reality to support teaching and learning. The results of the study show what is the distribution of curriculum content in virtual reality applications and what are the best users' rated educational virtual reality applications.

articleTitle: Soil sampling mobile platform for Agriculture 4.0
abstract: Soil testing is essential for modern agriculture: to optimise the production, protect the environment from fertilisers overuse, save money and energy during the production. The purpose of this work was to develop an autonomous mobile platform with soil sampling device for agriculture. Soil samples are analysed to determine the composition, characteristics or nutrient levels of the soil. Smallholder farmers can use simple hand-held field-testing kits. However, in the case of large farms where plants are grown upon hundreds of hectares, the autonomous mobile platform with a soil sampler would be the optimal solution. Precision farming is a concept of using new production and management methods that use all kind of data collected about specific locations and crop variety. The mentioned robot can increase resource and cost efficiency in acquiring the required data. Information about the soil properties can be retrieved from the field using the robot's onboard systems, enabling farmers to respond to abrupt changes in real time. Data technologies and collecting soil system allows an efficient production process. Use of robots on farms is associated with the progressive digitisation of all areas of our lives, and agriculture is no exception. After the presentation of available commercial solutions to soil sampling and data storage solutions, we will describe the core design of the mentioned soil sampling robot. The mobile robot has a form of a six-wheeled platform with the all-terrain suspension system. The soil sampling device is placed onboard and consists of a drill pipe with custom flap design on the end of it, to keep the soil within, preserving whole cross-section. The storage of soil samples and its analysis are currently being developed. Significant observations after tests and studies point out that such a robot could increase production efficiency. Collected samples provide accurate data of nutrient-supplying capacity.

articleTitle: Combining SMC and MTPA Using an EKF to Estimate Parameters and States of an Interior PMSM
abstract: This paper deals with an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF), which allows the estimation of nonlinear values of the permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM). A Sliding Mode Control (SMC) in an internal loop controls the optimal current with the estimated values of the EKF. The desired currents are calculated by a Maximum Torque Per Ampere (MTPA) strategy which works in the external loop of control.

articleTitle: Universal robot employment to mimic human writing
abstract: The paper presents an approach to design rapid and fluid movements of an universal robot to perform robot writing mimicking both the human kinematics when signing and the trajectory. To perform the task, on-line human signing standards are created first. Robot writing task is performed using these standards after that and robot signatures are acquired as a result. Next, both human and robot signatures are analyzed and compared, and the degree of signatures correlation is defined. Finally, recommendations of robot motion improvement are given.

articleTitle: Force and position control of the integrated electro-hydraulic servo-drive
abstract: Modern integrated electro-hydraulic servo-drives due to the complex integration of the hydraulic actuator, control valve, controller and sensors put high demands on their design and optimization. The integrated electro-hydraulic servo-drive (IEHSD) consists of a hydraulic actuator with position and force sensors. The hydraulic actuator (HA) is directly connected to a 4/3-way high response proportional directional control valve (4WRSE) with integrated axis controller (IAC). Integrated electro-hydraulic servo drives enable separate control of position, force and speed, combined force and position control, as well as control of motion synchronization of multiple drives. By synchronized motion control of integrated electro-hydraulic servo-drives, the trajectory tracking control of multi-axis manipulators with parallel structures is realized.

articleTitle: Frequency analysis of urban traffic noise
abstract: The paper presents the analysis results of vehicle traffic measurements which were used to simulate the noise measurands. The Cnossos-EU model were used for this purpose. The traffic flow was measured over the period between January and December 2013. The measurements were documented at one hour intervals throughout the entire 24 hours of the day (1:00-24:00). The results of noise simulations were compared with the equivalent sound level calculated by permanent automatic sound and traffic volume monitoring station. The frequency noise analysis was calculated according to the Cnossos-EU model. The results was described using parameters such as the median C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</sub>, average peak level C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">90</sub>, average background noise level C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub>, percentiles C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">25</sub> and C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">75</sub>. It was found that in most cases, the distribution of the tested variable was not normal. Analyzes carried out for the tested section of the road showed that the traffic of light motor - and medium heavy - vehicles is the main source of road noise. It has been shown that maximum values of the equivalent sound level occur for the frequency of 1000 Hz. The minimum values are in the octave band f0=125 Hz.

articleTitle: Design of Controllers Applied to Autonomous Unmanned Aerial Vehicles Using Software In The Loop
abstract: This paper presents the design of the altitude controller of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) based on the data acquired from the Software in the Loop (SITL). More specifically, the developed methodology permits to describe a test procedure where an algorithm or even a control strategy can be designed and validated based on the physical model of the system. In this way, the PID controller with a technique known as Successive Loop Closure is designed. The paper also shows how to establish a remote communication with the quadcopter using all the versatility of the Software in the Loop (SITL) in combination with a Ground Control Station and Dronekit developing tool. Finally, the flight simulation tests show that the designed controller was able to reach a stable flight with its performance evaluated through non-intrusive performance indexes and analysis of the system response in the time domain.

articleTitle: Bin Picking Success Rate Depending on Sensor Sensitivity
abstract: The goal of this contribution is to determine correlation between an applied sensor for object registration and the success rate of the bin-picking problem. In most applications of a bin picking problem in industry, the procedure consists of two consecutive steps. The first step provides an initial guess of both position and rotation angle of the object to be registered, while the second one improves the exact pose accuracy, as required in following tasks. The second step can be, among others, implemented by the Iterative Closest Point Algorithm (ICP). It is well known that the ICP algorithm is very sensitive to the initial guess of the position and rotation angle of the object. Another interesting feature, especially from the technicians point of view, is the sensitivity of the ICP algorithm in relation to the applied sensor. Therefore, one particular bin picking application, involving complex irregular objects, is examined in this paper. Various kinds of sensors for 3D scene reconstruction are employed and, as a result of this contribution, a comprehensive set of relations between sensor quality and the ICP algorithm sensitivity is formulated.

articleTitle: Standard, Parallel and Series Two Degree of Freedom PID Controllers
abstract: The paper deals with standard, parallel and series two degree of freedom PID controllers. It is shown that these controllers can be presented in three identical structures. This idea is new. There are given relations which allow mutual conversion of their adjustable parameters and setpoint weights. The application is illustrated on the example.

Author Keywords: two degree of freedom PID controllers

articleTitle: 2DOF PI Controller Tuning for Integrating Plants with the Setting of Setpoint Weight
abstract: This paper is dealing with controllers tuning of analog and discrete two degree of freedom PI (2DOF PI) controllers with chosen methods for integrating plants. The focus is to determine optimal weight of the 2DOF PI controller to achieve better quality of control process and reduce overshoot. Results are shown on the examples.

articleTitle: On Mitigation of Four-Wave Mixing in High Capacity Ultra-DWDM System
abstract: Due to the excessive demand on multimedia, the network traffic requires new technologies to improve communication networks. The core data networks are formed of single and multichannel fiber optical transmission systems nowadays. The leading technology in a multichannel fiber optical communication is 10 Gbps DWDM (Dense Wavelength Division Multiplexing), which is used worldwide. The 40 Gbps DWDM systems are still in the adaptation phase. The development of DWDM system increases the transmission speed, transmission distance and channel traffic. On the other hand, the multichannel transmission over single optical fiber induces nonlinear effects which degrades performance of DWDM system. The four-wave mixing (FWM) is the most dominant of all nonlinear effects, especially in dense division multiplexing systems. FWM appear as a crosstalk between the adjacent channels in DWMD system. In this paper we propose a strategy to mitigate the impact of FWM on optical signal transmission in a DQPSK modulated 32-channel Ultra-DWDM system with 1.28 Tbps (40 Gbps per channel) transmission capacity. The simulation model is based on the ITU-T G.694.1 and created in OptiSystem™ software. The resulting signal is mathematically analyzed and BER and Q factor values are calculated.

articleTitle: A Fuzzy Expert Model for Availability Evaluation
abstract: Each technical system within itself carries the great potential danger of possible occurrence of failure and damages. Mining machines are characteristic by great investment values, costs of unplanned shutdowns, complex working conditions, and environment and workers hazards. Systematic monitoring of the mining machinery is of great importance for the management of the mining companies. Availability is the overall concept of quality of service. Includes information regarding the operating state, an idle state, a standby state and shut down. The availability can be calculated by the time coefficient, which includes mention time state. For time state tracking, specific IT structure is necessary. Such a structure is often very expensive and unavailable. An alternative is the expert system, which can absorb partial indicators of the availability, including their uncertainty, diversity, relativity. In this article, an expert's fuzzy model is presented to analyze and integrate reliability, maintainability, and functionality of three types of bulldozers that operate at the lignite mines. In the end, a comparison of the bulldozers is done. Conclusions can be used for maintenance, in logistics and during the purchasing of new machines.

articleTitle: Ant Colony Optimization Algorithm and Artificial Immune System Applied to a Robot Route
abstract: This Article aims to introduce two meta-heuristics techniques: Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) and Artificial Immune System (AIS) to find the best route for a robot. The ACO is an algorithm based on the ant food search process, and the AIS is inspired by the defending mechanism of the human organism. In order to illustrate and compare the potential of these techniques, this paper applies both techniques in a problem of determining the shortest possible route for a robot without hitting any obstacles in three different maps. According to the tests, the ACO shows better results regarding the number of iterations to reach the global optimum, while the AIS shows better results when it comes to the processing time. From the result, it can be seen that the ACO found a solution to all maps demonstrating it is an excellent choice for this problem type.

articleTitle: IoT Solution for Assessing the Indoor Air Quality of Educational Facilities
abstract: The indoor air quality and other environmental factors of education facilities, such as university lecture halls and dormitories, has been brought up lately as a factor severely influencing learning outcome. It was found also, that air quality metrics, such as CO2 level, temperature, humidity, noise, and illumination are far from optimal in facilities having sensor networks capable of capable of measuring such parameters, and in some cases, they are out of the range allowed by national standards. Unfortunately, there is very limited data available, and it is possible, that this problem is wide scale, but currently the lack of low-cost solutions to monitor these parameters makes it very hard to assess the situation. In the paper, we present an environmental monitoring solution based on the Internet of Things (IoT) paradigm, primarily for educational facilities, which can reproduce the system with minimal investment. The system based on low-cost Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) wireless sensor boards and BLE-WIFI gateway using a ubiquitous single board computer (SBC) board. The software components are open source, as the BLE sensor board software is available from the manufacturer as an application example, the SBC uses Linux, and our software will be available as free, open-source software. The system does not only monitor these environmental parameters but can provide feedback for the occupants of the facility using LEDs on the sensor boars. We are going to present our preliminary results showing the applicability of our solution.

articleTitle: Design of Digital CAN Based Car Dashboard Unit
abstract: The paper describes the design and implementation of the CAN based digital dashboard unit used in the design study SCE of the electric car. The system consists of a CAN communication interface unit based on a PIC microcontroller and graphic programmable LCD displays. The work is not only described in terms of technical solution, but also in terms of design.

articleTitle: Signal-Based Approach to EMG-Sensor Fault Detection in Upper Limb Prosthetics
abstract: Electromyography (EMG) signals have been extensively used as a control signal in robotics, rehabilitation and health care. Creating an prosthetic hand requires many steps, beginning with a way for the prosthesis to detect the EMG signal. Unfortunately, signal detection may cause some troubles. Among them there are sensor faults that may lead to serious distortion of the signal and malfunction of the prosthetic hand. This paper is devoted to the development of algorithmic software that allows to detect faults of EMG sensors of prosthetic hand. To solve the problem modules of fault detection and signal correction were developed. These modules not only carefully supervise records from individual EMG electrodes, but, if necessary, replace them in systems if one or more signals are violated. This approach is based on signal processing methods with low computational complexity, that allows to reduce hardware requirements.

articleTitle: Utilization of the Mathematical Model of the Converter Process for the Sensitivity Analysis
abstract: The contribution deals with the proposal and realization of the mathematical model of the converter process. In the introduction are described processes of formation of the metal batch, slag, converter gas and blowing oxygen consumption as well as material and heat balance of the converter process. In the next an algorithm and implementation of the mathematical model is described. Finally, simulation results are presented and the sensitivity analysis of selected inputs to the steel temperature is realized.

articleTitle: A DNP3-based SCADA Architecture Supporting Electronic Signatures
abstract: Security of industrial control systems is a well-known issue, and it has become stringent given the vulnerabilities of the widely available, modern communication technologies, and new paradigms such as Internet of Things. Another related issue concerns the redundancy of an interconnected industrial system, while distributing the data processing capabilities in separated physical or geographical components of a SCADA-based system. Our paper deals with some of the security issues, within the Distributed Network Protocol (DNP3). In the context of Intelligent Electronic Devices acting as Remote Terminal Units (RTU), we have studied the ways in which data integrity and data-origin authentication is handled in SCADA architectures, and found that the benefits offered by electronic signatures can be incorporated within such architectures, while preserving the performance criteria. Modern RTUs are capable to handle networks of sensors, to fusion their acquired data and deliver this data through a secure communication line to a master terminal unit. We have proposed a new architectural solution by modifying the Link Protocol Data Unit of DNP3, such that support for data integrity and data-origin authentication is ensured by means of electronic signature.

articleTitle: Electric Cars in the Czech Republic – The Analysis of CO2 Emissions Reduction
abstract: The actual trend in the automotive industry is to discover electric vehicles and bring them to the market in a few years. There are some pilot products in electric cars production and still a lot of open questions connected with this new type of power source for vehicles. This article tries to answer at least to questions related to pollution and ecology. The comparative study and analysis of diesel engine vehicles and electric engine vehicles are made. The analysis is focused on an overall car production emission trace and lifetime emission trace. The global warming potential is calculated for gasoline/diesel engine car and comparable electrical engine car. The study is focused on vehicles driven in the Czech Republic. The vehicle operation area/country is an important factor in all emission calculation because electric car emissions depend on the type of power plant primary source and highlight the need for pollution friendly power sources.

articleTitle: Optimizing Algorithms for low CPU Usage in Different Scenarios
abstract: This paper proposes a series of results over the image processing algorithms and for the shortest path algorithm that influence the percentage of CPU utilization. Starting with the fractal generation to image analysis, compression for big images and also any algorithm, the parallel programing is today one of the most important factor for low consumption and good power balanced for the processing unit. A good balance between the processing capacity, the algorithm and the time of processing is hard to obtain due to the number of calculus. In this work a series of results and comparison between sequential and parallel algorithms are presented. Also, there are presented test scenarios in different cases that confirm or infirm the parallel strategy chosen. This paper will integrate the results obtained with the proposed algorithms reports or comparisons of the proposed parallelization methods and will provide conclusions and ideas for future research in this field with extensive uses.

articleTitle: Impact of PZT layer properties in a cantilever beam on energy harvesting performance
abstract: The paper presents results of numerical parametric analysis of an energy harvester based on the construction of cantilever beam. The device has two-layered section made of polymer substrate and piezoelectric ceramic PZT as an active layer. A determination of an impact of harvester operating parameters (resistance and excitation amplitude), PZT layer thickness and PZT type on electrical output of the beam and maximum stress values in both layers was the aim of conducted numerical analysis. Performed numerical analyses allow to choose selected parameters values of given cantilever beam harvester which make it possible to receive the most preferable results in the field of material stress and generated electrical energy.

articleTitle: Robust Control of a Two-Axis Gimbaled Seeker Using Loop Shaping Design Procedure
abstract: A two-axis gimbaled seeker must stabilize the gimbal axis in the inertial plane from the missile body motion disturbances. The missile guidance performance to the aiming target in the terminal homing phase depends significantly on the control performances of a two-axis gimbaled seeker. A two-degree of freedom robust control formulation is suggested for improving the control performances of a two-axis gimbaled seeker. The simulation results confirm the validity of the two-degree of freedom robust control formulation by evaluating several control performances of the two-axis gimbaled seeker. The suggested two-degree of freedom robust controller achieves the best control performances and robust stability among controllers to be introduced for comparison.

articleTitle: Wind Turbine Tower-Nacelle System with MR Tuned Vibration Absorber: Modelling, Test Rig, and Identification
abstract: The paper concerns a wind turbine tower-nacelle system equipped with magnetorheological (MR) damper based tuned vibration absorber (TVA). The analytical and simulation models of the considered physical system, as well as the laboratory test rig, including data acquisition and control environment, are all described. The identification procedure of the regarded laboratory model using FEM updating technique is presented. The experimental and simulation frequency responses are compared. This paper is a first section of a two-part model identification study.

articleTitle: Process Control with IIoT Capabilities of the Hollow Cathode Plasma Nitriding
abstract: This paper deals with the design and implementation of the process control software for the hollow cathode plasma nitriding system. An integrated monitoring, control and IIoT (Industrial Internet of Things) capable system was designed to fulfill the requirements of a modern industrial control system. Besides the new control tasks imposed by the hollow cathode plasma nitriding, the integration of the plasma diagnostics and the Ethernet based monitoring system was added to the process control system, thus online monitoring, remote access, data storing in cloud was developed. The paper is dedicated to the monitoring, data logging and remote control of the system, the controller design is not the current subject.

articleTitle: Description of using different software tools to analyze the selected process
abstract: Collecting a large amount of data of selected processes is a relatively simple task. It depends on the selection of the monitored parameters and the applications of the respective measuring members. However, the important step is to decide what to do with the obtained data, what information is relevant and what results are expected. In this contribution is considered set of measured data of the heating process consisting of several monitored parameters recorded at selected time intervals. The most typical parameters are: outdoor and indoor temperature, heat consumption, gas consumption, temperature and flow of heating medium or other parameters. There is an industrial control system used for visualization and control of industrial technologies and building automation, which allows the monitoring, storage and export of data in a suitable format for further processing. The aim of the paper is to compare the tools of two diametrically different software tools MS Excel and Matlab in terms of visualization, processing and evaluation of exported process data.

articleTitle: On Robust Performance Analysis of Linear Systems with Polytopic Uncertainties Affected by Random Disturbances
abstract: In this paper, linear discrete-time systems with polytopic uncertainties affected by random external disturbances are under consideration. The input disturbance is supposed to be a stochastic signal with known mean anisotropy which stands for “spectral color” of the signal. The anisotropic norm of the system indicates its stochastic gain from the input disturbance with the same mean anisotropy level to the output of the system. The problem is to find conditions which allow to check whether the uncertain system is stable and to estimate its performance index subject to input disturbance for all possible uncertainties. In order to solve this problem, Lyapunov functions technique and matrix inequalities approach are used to obtain the numerically effective procedure. To illustrate the efficiency of the proposed conditions, a numerical example is considered.

articleTitle: Semi-active reduction of device casing vibration using a set of piezoelectric elements
abstract: Semi-active control methods are well known in context of structural vibration reduction. Despite of lower efficiency in comparison to the active methods, they are still the alternatives providing several advantages. The main benefit is that no additional energy is added to the system, which guarantees stability of the whole system. In addition, semi-active methods are more efficient than passive ones, especially for the systems controlled by e.g. switching or adaptive algorithms and with non-stationary excitation or unknown excitation during the design stage. The experiments have been performed using five Macro Fiber Composite piezoelectric elements attached to a thin, steel plate, which is a front wall of a cubical, rigid casing. The placement of the elements has been optimized based on the measured mode shapes of the structure. The vibration of other walls are reduced using the passive methods. This paper is focused on experimental evaluation of structural vibration reduction, depending on excitation and configuration of piezoelectric elements. Several types of electrical circuits are considered.

articleTitle: Validation Of Cnossos-EU Urban Traffic Noise Model
abstract: The results of vehicle traffic measurements were used to simulate the equivalent sound level of urban noise. The Cnossos-EU model was used for this purpose. The traffic flow was measured over the period between January and December 2013. The measurements were documented at one-hour intervals throughout the entire 24 hours of the day (1:00-24:00). The results of noise simulations were compared with the equivalent sound level calculated by permanent automatic sound and traffic volume monitoring station. The results obtained for the data recorded on working days were compared. The dispersion of the equivalent sound level was described using the positional measures. The analysis consisted of the Jarque-Bera and the Shapiro-Wilk tests for the recorded and calculated data were conducted. The results indicated that in almost all cases, the distribution of the tested variable was not normal. Box plots were used to assess whether outliers data occurred in the recorded results. The analysis of the recorded and calculated data was performed for three time sub-intervals of a 24-hour interval: day, evening, and night.

articleTitle: Neural Network Control for Robot Manipulator
abstract: The basic issue discussed in the engineering work is to get acquainted with the structure and construction of neural networks and the principle of their operation. The whole process was discussed as well as selected methods of learning neural networks. The next part of the work presents a review of artificial neural networks in the direction of their application to control nonlinear systems used in automation. In the next chapter the model of nonlinear system was describes in detail. A manipulator simulator was created in the Matlab / Simulink program. Two controllers: a neural controller and the most commonly used PID controller have been implemented to control a nonlinear system. Controllers were evaluated for the quality of work and compared the influence of a given regulators on the control of a nonlinear system in terms of selected criteria.

articleTitle: Automated system for optimizing input parameters of the UCG process
abstract: The paper continues to post on the contributions published at previous ICCC conferences in 2016 and 2017. The optimization of input oxidizers was solved in three variants of objective function - maximizing calorific value, minimizing unburned carbon and complex optimization criterion, for different thermodynamic temperatures. This paper describes the design and verification of an automated system for optimizing input parameters. This system makes it possible to optimize the choice of different types of optimality criteria, to set a different initial estimate of input oxidants. The core of the system is a modified gradient method. The automated system was created and programming in the DELPHI software.

articleTitle: Arrival air traffic separations assessment using Maximum Likelihood Estimation and Fisher Information Matrix
abstract: This article presents method for analysis of selected aspects of arrival air traffic by fitting past arrival air traffic data to one of known continuous probability distributions, with use of maximum likelihood estimation method and Fisher Information Matrix. Data modelling in the analyzed form of continuous probability distribution allows for quantitative assessment of that data. Presented work focuses on analysis of aircraft separations in the final part of descent, where all arriving aircraft should have maintained required separation values. Motivation for the research, modelling assumptions, mathematical model, and sample scenarios are presented in the article. Selected scenarios cover variety of possible arrival air traffic distributions over time, including low and high arrival air traffic intensity cases. Results present that proposed method can be used in air traffic management, especially for analysis of past arrival air traffic data, in order to build predictive models for future arrival traffic modelling.

articleTitle: SCARA robot control based on Raspberry Pi
abstract: The article presents a construction project of a SCARA robot with a control system based on a Raspberry Pi microcontroller. The structure and exemplary results of strength analysis of some parts are presented. Reverse kinematics calculations were presented and the working space was determined. Control algorithm, its possibilities and ways of modification are described.

articleTitle: Impact of a carrying layer properties on stress in a multilayer piezoelectric harvester
abstract: Energy harvesters of cantilever beam construction and methods of improving its performance are topic of many publications. Among numerous propositions for enhancing energy output or durability of a beam generator is, for example, modification of its general shape or expanding whole system by adding additional masses, springs or dampers. However, at the same time, carrying layer material is often overlooked. Following Euler-Bernoulli beam theory, for given beam deflection, material of carrying layer does not have any influence on piezoelectric layers. Yet, employment of FEM simulation allows to obtain more accurate results which show how actually material of a carrying layer can affect bordering piezoelectric layer. This paper presents results of numerical calculations which assess influence of a carrying layer material, described by a Young modulus and Poisson ratio, on the amount of strain energy and maximum value of stress in piezoelectric layer of a beam harvester.

articleTitle: Experimental and numerical investigation of the active double wishbone suspension system
abstract: The paper presents research results of wheeled vehicle double wishbone suspension strut with electrohydraulic actuator. Frequency characteristics and performance indexes of the suspension system were determined. The results were compared with the passive commercial suspension system of the same vehicle. The transmissibility function, tire deflection function, clearance function were taken into consideration in order to compare suspension systems. The laboratory research was performed on the test stand with the electrohydraulic exciter in order to simulate road irregularities. The tests were performed by using different classes of excitation. Road surface profile classification according to norm “ISO 8608 Mechanical vibration - Road surface profiles - Reporting of measured data” was considered. The influence of the actuator dynamics on the suspension system performance was investigated.

articleTitle: Nonlinear modeling and parameter identification for electro-hydraulic servo system
abstract: The article concerns the modeling and identification of parameters of nonlinear systems described by the Hammerstein model with asymmetrical static nonlinearities. The possibilities of applying dynamic identification with a discrete linear model in the evaluation of the dynamics of electro-hydraulic servo-drive are presented. This assessment is of key importance when designing modern power or positioning control systems. Experimental data is used to determine the dynamics of the real system model and to estimate the unknown parameters of the model. The article presents selected results of current identification tests of the electro-hydraulic servo system, as a result of which a discrete parametric model of object was derived.

articleTitle: Detection Time Analysis of Propulsion System Fault Effects in a Hexacopter
abstract: The hexacopter propulsion system is composed of electronic speed controllers, motors and propellers. When severe damage happens in one of these components, critical impacts over the system's dynamics are witnessed. Changing the controller parameters or even adopting a different control strategy is useless once the system loses its controllability. To prevent significant damages, this work presents a case study about the detection time effects that total faults interfere with the aircraft dynamics, which is extremely necessary to be identified and perceived by the aircraft control board. The case study was built using nonintrusive indices, based on an error from angular dynamics responses. Once identified a failure situation, a future control device can provide some performance actions due to critical issues, without losing the aircraft controllability or leaving it to crash. The results were impressive, showing that it is possible to develop fault detection and identification technique in 0.1 seconds tops, keeping the aircraft safe in these scenarios. Longer detection time may lead to insert non-controllable cases.

articleTitle: The impact of changes in operating parameters on the bag filter in the WR - 25 water boiler
abstract: The publication presents the impact of changes in operating parameters on the bag filter in the WR - 25 water boiler. This paper shows the solution of the water boiler control process implemented by changing the work regime of the bag filter. It was obtained by modifying the settings of the bag filter automation. Due to the increasing requirements of flue gas cleanliness, it is necessary to use increasingly new and more efficient flue gas cleaning installations. One of such solutions is a fabric bag filter. In the study, the boiler is equipped with an automated handling SCADA system expanded to control bag filter. At the beginning, this solution resulted in accelerated destruction of most of the bag filters despite the proper operation of the bag filter in automatic mode. Analysis of the boiler, heating network and bag filters operation allowed to find the solution for the problem by changing the operating regime of the bag filters resulting from the modification of the settings of the bag filter automatics.

articleTitle: The impact of selected priority rules on production goals
abstract: The paper presents the outcome of a study that dealt with scheduling of operations and in particular with the impact of selected priority rules on production goals. The impact of the priority rules was examined on a simulation model of the smart flexible manufacturing system with interchangeable workplaces. These problems are characterized as job shop scheduling problems. The study documents the influence of the five selected priority rules FIFO (First in First out), EDD (Earliest Due Date), STR (Slack Time Remaining), STR/OP (Slack Time Remaining per Operation) and SQNO (Shortest Queue at the Next Operation) on chosen production objectives. The effect of applied priority rule has been studied at a different production system loading. The evaluation of experimental results and their synthesis conduce to the formulation of knowledge for the real use of these priority rules in the scheduling of operations.

articleTitle: Influence of Temperature on the MR Squeeze-Mode Damper
abstract: In the paper the authors present the results of a numerical study involving a magnetorheological (MR) fluid damper operating in squeeze-mode. The study is an attempt to analyze both heat generation and heat dissipation mechanisms within the device. In this numerical experiment an exemplary squeeze-mode device is evaluated for temperature changes resulting from mechanical and electrical inputs, respectively. We solve the resulting model based on the Stefan model, and then couple it with a lumped parameter model of the electromagnetic circuit of the actuator. In the resulting analysis the model is subjected to various types of mechanical and electrical stimuli, respectively. Finally, we present the numerical results for temperature rise and force fading.

articleTitle: Time and Frequency Domain Description of Gilbert-Elliott Data Loss Models
abstract: Nowadays, the usage radio channel or Internet connection grows for real-time transmission of measurement data or signals. For these applications, not reliable communication needs to be analyzed from a signal processing point of view. Our paper contributes to this topic with the analysis of data loss as a signal distorting phenomenon. The paper contains a possible mathematical description of the data loss via the indicator function. Moreover, the Gilbert-Elliott data loss model class is presented, which gives a framework to analyse numerous data loss phenomena in general. In order to analyse the data loss in the frequency domain, the spectrum of the indicator function is required. This paper presents the derivation of the power spectral density of the Gilbert-Elliott model. The paper reviews a possible identification method for the simpler models derived from the Gilbert-Elliott model. Theoretical analysis and simulations are supported by measurements. The measurement results are used to show how the data loss models function in practice.

articleTitle: Shifting method for relay feedback identification implemented in PLC Tecomat
abstract: This paper presents the first practical use of a new method called “shifting method” for relay feedback identification of dynamic systems. This recently published method enables estimating up to three points on a frequency characteristics of dynamic systems from data observed by one relay experiment. This approach was used for parameter estimation of second order plus dead time model and for PID controller autotuning. The Mosaic programming environment was used for implementat this method to the PLC Tecomat Foxtrot. The code is written in the Structured Text language. Proposed technique applicability was tested both on simulated systems and two real systems.

articleTitle: Preparation of 3D models of Trucks for Timber Load Analysis
abstract: The article describes a unique method of processing scanned point cloud on a moving object with variable speed. Point clouds represent a set of trucks loaded by a scanning gate made up of four 2D laser scanners. Three scanners record the surface of the truck from three sides, the fourth scanner records the longitudinal change of the profile of one of a truck's side. From this profile, the method evaluates the motion movement function by which all other point clouds are recalculated. The result is a modified point clouds representing the surface of the standing set. The article also provides a way of point segmentation that separates the points representing the timber load from the truck.

articleTitle: Feedback Control of Robot Manipulators by Using Gravity and Inertial Effects Compensation
abstract: The paper describes an approach to the robot manipulator control based on a compensation of non-linear gravity terms and inertial terms in the robot motion equations and applying the PD or PID-type control law. While benefits of the compensation of the gravity force effects are well known, the inertial effects compensation, which seems to be more difficult to implement, brings additional enhancement of the control quality. An approximate compensation can be carried out in a relatively simple and efficient way, if the robot dynamics is represented by a mass-point model. The remaining influences can be treated as disturbances. Unlike the inverse dynamics approach, complete and precise mathematical model of the robot is not needed, which is an important advantage, since models of robots containing more than three links are usually very complex and difficult to obtain.

articleTitle: Exploitation of EMG Signals for Video Game Control
abstract: Nowadays, the video games industry has many types of controllers to offer. This paper aims to explore the potential of utilizing electromyography as another device for video games control. In this paper the whole flow of EMG signal processing have been disused and examined. Signal filters have been designed and tested. For hand gestures classification have been build a neural network model which was trained and tested using different features achieved by using some metrics combination and wavelet decomposition. Built classifier was used to control a simple game.

articleTitle: Series Two Degree of Freedom PID Controller for Integrating Plants with Time Delay
abstract: The paper is devoted to the series two degree of freedom PID controller. The conversion relations for controller adjustable parameters and for setpoint weights are given. Fully analytical multiple dominant pole method for tuning and setpoint weights selecting is used. The use is shown on the example.

Author Keywords: series two degree of freedom PID controller

articleTitle: Analysis of a closed loop system with DC micro-motor electrical drive with propeller and variable- fractional order PID controller
abstract: In this paper a closed loop system with DC micro-motor electrical drive with propeller and variable- fractional order PID angular velocity controller is analyzed. As a plant mathematical model one takes fractional order linear time-invariant commensurate difference equation with a nonlinear static feedback. In the model a fractional order Grnwald Let-nikov backward difference is applied. In the analysis a novelty description of the closed-loop system is used. As a performance criterion of the closed loop system error one takes the Integral Square Error. The variable- fractional order PID controller is tuned to minimize the closed loop system error when the external disturbance (the external torque) is zero or nonzero. The investigations are supported by numerical examples.

articleTitle: Cooperative Cheap Automated Guided Vehicles
abstract: The industrial environment in which independent platforms have to ensure the transfer of semi-finished products is dense in events. Elimination of collision's possibilities, blockages related to possible defects or supply problems would provide a significant increase in production line productivity. Cheap Automated Guided Vehicles (CAGV) will lead to even more agglomeration of work space, which requires collaborative communication between systems. This article addresses the implementation of a communication module between the experimental CAGV s that have been made so that collisions can be prevented, but also the transfer speed can be adapted to the change of workflow at master's request. At the end of the article are presented the possibilities of expanding the communication capabilities between CAGV at the level of an enterprise that falls within the concept of Industry 4.0.

articleTitle: Electronic Steering With Force Feedback
abstract: The paper describes the design and implementation of the electronic steering wheel control system with force feedback. The main purpose of this project is the development of a steering wheel unit for the implementation of “steer-by-wire” technology or as a basis for the autonomous vehicles control. The work includes construction of a steering wheel unit with use of DC motor and the design of an electronics for its control.

articleTitle: Locomotion Solution for Stair Climbing Wheelchair with ER Fluid Based Control
abstract: Wheelchairs for people with disabilities are generally intended for movement on dedicated or arranged terrains. Stair climbing or uneven terrain is a real challenge. Current models use two methods to overcome this problem. The first method is to move with the mixed wheels/tracks. The tracks are used for movement on stairs or rough terrain and wheels in the rest of the cases. The second method uses multiple wheels to solve the staircase issue. In this paper the authors propose a wheelchair whose wheels have variable geometry. When the stairs or rough terrain type appears, the wheels change their geometry by adjusting to the ground. Practically the wheelchair wheel is made up of slices/spokes that can extend linearly and controlled, along the wheel's rays. Thus, the contour of the wheel can be modeled so that it becomes the negative of the ground, and the movement of the seat is made along some curves or linear trajectories. The actuator used for the wheel extension is a hybrid structure combining a spring-type actuator with a rheological hydraulic piston. For extension of wheel spokes the spring action is used. The retraction of the wheel elements is made by trough of the weight of the wheelchair. The control of the extension and retraction of the wheel spokes are made through by the control of a rheological piston. In the paper is also presented the control algorithm for movement to a known topometry field.

articleTitle: Algorithm for Early Warning System for Contamination in Water Network
abstract: The Water Network Tool for Resilience (WNTR) library, running on hydraulic models developed in EPANET, was first published in 2017. It allows not only hydraulic and quality simulations but also modeling of events such as power outages, pipe breaks, incidental contamination events, earthquakes and other unusual situations that may occur in water supply networks. This article presents the practical application of this algorithm (quoted in the title) in an Early Warning System (EWS). Based on a selected hydraulic model of a water supply network and a random dose of some contamination, the role of this algorithm is to propose which sections of the network should be closed to minimize the contamination impact. Additionally, this paper discusses how the use of WNTR tool may help to influence follow-up reactions in case of the type of event having been described.

articleTitle: Experimental research of the controllable suspension strut
abstract: This paper provides an essential approach of investigation of the front suspension of Sport Utility Vehicle (SUV) with a MacPherson strut. The original shock absorber was modified and a prototype hydraulic damper was used with the ability to control the damping force during compression and rebound. On the basis of laboratory tests, the static characteristics of the shock absorber prototype and dynamic suspension strut were determined in relation to the original vehicle suspension. The suspension system was forced by external excitation pretended to irregularities for various road classes in accordance with the ISO 8608 standard. For these tests, assessment indices of selected suspension quality parameters were determined.

articleTitle: Parking House Action Subsystem Control
abstract: This article solves action subsystem control of a multi-storey underground automatic parking house model, which was developed as a solution for automatic vehicle parking. The model operation is provided by a distributed system consisting of microcontroller units at two levels. Both levels communicate with each other via serial UART communication. The algorithm controls the linear two-stage dual-sided telescopic mechanism and a two-axis positioning mechanism. The emphasis is placed on the smooth movement of all axes which limits shocks caused by mechanism speed change while moving to a defined position.

articleTitle: Time-Driven Sub-GHz Wireless Communication Protocol for Real-Time Cyber-Physical Systems
abstract: Application of wireless communication solutions grows in Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS), even if the CPS must fulfill real-time requirements. However, nearly all of these solutions use the ubiquitous 2.4/5 GHz ISM frequency bands (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, etc.) or licensed frequency bands for mobile operators (2G/3G/4G, NB-IoT, etc.). In most applications these solutions are used even if they are not real-time, i.e., they cannot provide the synchronization, delay, and reliability requirements brought up by these applications. There are other wireless solutions for the lower 433 MHz or 868/933 MHz (depending on the geographic location) bands, but their use is limited, even if these frequencies provide much better propagation properties, longer range, can be operated using less power, etc. LoRa and Sigfox use these frequency bands, however, they provide only low data rate services, which are also without any guarantee for real-time operation. On the other hand, due to the simplicity and low complexity radio chips available, it is also possible to adapt these radios for specialized protocols. In the paper, we present a wireless radio protocol for 868 MHz ISM frequency band that provides microsecond range synchronization error, guaranteed delay, and clear message reliability schematics. The protocol is based on an IEEE 1588 derived clock synchronization and time-division multiple access communication scheme. The protocol is demonstrated in a simple application also, in which both time synchronization and low delay guaranteed message delivery are essential for successful operation.

articleTitle: Extending the Takagi-Sugeno hierarchical expert system for the system for evaluating competencies
abstract: This paper describes an improved hierarchical Takagi-Sugeno expert system which is based on the proposed expert system published earlier. This approach is intended to be effectively applied in a system that evaluates professional competencies of people (job applicants, employees). The previous proposed system works with any number of competencies which were represented by their percentage evaluation and their importance from the predetermined scale. The result of this expert system was the overall competencies evaluation of the given person (towards the job position) and the whole hierarchical evaluation was visually shown to the user. The extended version of this expert system has another input. It is a binary attribute that determines whether the competency is mandatory. If the person does not meet the compulsory competency (0% rating), the rating of the pair (where the pair occurs) is automatically rated 0%. Another mechanism used here is the transmission of this zero result in the next part of the hierarchy. Thus, if the job applicant or employee has unfulfilled one compulsory competency, the total result is 0% in the final evaluation of the applicant. However, HR managers have a visualisation of the whole evaluation process, so they know which competency or competencies caused this result.

articleTitle: A temperature control system for laser welding of plastics differing in optical parameters
abstract: This article describes a specially developed system for automatic control of temperature in the weld area during lap welding. The major aim of the system is to hold the required temperature constant while joining two plastic materials differing in optical properties, where one part is transparent to the laser radiation and the other absorbs it. The system uses a real-time reconfigurable National Instruments CompactRio controller featuring conditioned input-output modules. The control application, based on fuzzy logic control, was created using LabVIEW software. A sampling rate of 1kHz was employed. The feedback signal is derived from an optical pyrometer, which measures the temperature in the fusion zone. The study involved empirically determining the optimal settings and testing the controller performance. The article includes waveform data concerning the process variable, the control signal and the error signal.

articleTitle: IAE minimization in sliding mode control for second order systems with velocity constraint
abstract: This paper comprises the design of the terminal sliding mode controller, which drives the representative point of the system to the demand state in finite time. Our goal is to obtain the robustness with respect to perturbations. Therefore, we eliminate the reaching phase by selecting a non-linear, non-stationary switching line. Parameters of that sliding line are selected to limit the system's velocity from above by a predefined constant and from below by its additive inverse. To obtain a good dynamics of our system we minimize the IAE (Integral Absolute Error) quality index.

articleTitle: On the Analysis and Tool Development of the Long Term Evolution Cell Planning
abstract: As the countdown to the 5G revolution has begun, the deployment of desirable non-standalone 5G new radio networks will necessarily demand to be built based on well-planned and optimized existing LTE networks. Mobile Network planning reduces the network flaws, maintenance operations and wasted resources, leading to minimising the pre-deployment and post-deployment cost. This paper includes coverage and capacity planning for long-term evolution networks, implemented in a tool using C# programming. In coverage planning part we conducted the detailed link budget analysis to obtain the maximum allowable path loss on the radio link. After that, we studied propagation models and used it in calculating cell size. In the end, we performed mathematical calculations to find the number of needed cells for the coverage. The capacity planning part deals with studying the requirements in the network, to meet the needed data speeds for different services such as VoIP, video calls and conferences, real-time gaming, streaming and web browsing. We used the service models, and traffic models approach to estimate the single-user average throughput during the network busy hour. Then we calculated the cell average throughput, determined the physical layer specifications, and finally, we ended up with obtaining the number of cells for capacity considerations.

articleTitle: Control System Design for a Walking beam furnace
abstract: Walking beam furnaces belong to industry furnace group with a high energy consumption before rolling processes. The main goal of these furnaces is to ensure a uniform billets heating so that rolling is successful at the required performance and quality in the rolling mill. The main reason of reduced quality heating billet is the non-uniform distribution of temperature over the charge length. In proposed paper will be analysed this problem by mathematical model and solved by suitable decentralized control system. The Auto Regressive-Moving-Average method (ARMAX) model has been used for identification of the fuel stream and controllers were tuned with modified Ziegler-Nichols method for more regulation zones.

articleTitle: Parametric Optimization of a Second Order Time Delay System with a PD-Controller
abstract: The article addresses the parametric optimization problem for time delay system of second order with a PD controller. In the paper is considered the performance index of integral of squared error. The index value is equal to the value of the quadratic Lyapunov functional at initial function. One determines the quadratic Lyapunov functional of time delay system using the Lyapunov matrix. In the article the optimization outcomes for varies values of delay and for varies damping factor are given.

articleTitle: Variable-order PI Control Algorithm with Order Scheduled According to the Control Error and Anti-windup Strategy
abstract: In this paper, a control strategy based on variable order integrator is presented. The control strategy assumes that the order of the integrator depends on the control error which is divided into arbitrary number of intervals. Additionally, when control signal exceed limits, the variable order anti-windup strategy is applied by setting order to zero. For these strategies orders are assigned during numerical optimization. Results obtained for different types of variable order derivative (integral) definitions (A,B,D,E-types) are compared and analyzed.

Author Keywords: variable order derivatives PID control anti-windup algorithm

articleTitle: Controlling an industrial robotic system based on received visual information
abstract: This work presents a solution of the problem of controlling an industrial robotic system based on visual information received from a stereo camera that monitors robots workcell. Fully functional process of extracting an objects pose information is described. The additional functions which maintain and improve the recognition process in the case of multiple objects presented in the workcell are proposed. Further, a camera-robot system in which the above mentioned process is implemented is described.

articleTitle: Robust LMI Based Control of Magnetic Levitation Laboratory Plant
abstract: The paper presents robust pole placement controller design for a Magnetic Levitation System (MLS) from Inteco. The design constraints are considered to define desired closed-loop pole region locations. LMI region approach for a robust pole placement is adopted for a discrete-time case. Appropriate approximation of LMI region for the prescribed damping is discussed to meet the performance improvement requirements defined for a Magnetic Levitation system. The obtained results are illustrated on simulations as well as real laboratory plant.

articleTitle: Evolutionary Algorithm Based Multisine Inputs
abstract: This paper concerns the multisine power spectrum optimization and its influence on the system identification accuracy. For comparison purposes two kinds of manoeuvres were analysed. In the first case multisine inputs based on uniform power spectrum were designed. In the second case the amount of energy stored in each harmonic was optimized. This was achieved by minimizing the Relative Peak Factor and allowed to obtain multisine inputs with non-uniform power spectrum. Both designs were used later to excite the object. The aircraft response was registered and used for estimating stability and control derivatives. To perform the parameter estimation Output Error Method was selected. The evaluations were performed in Matlab environment.

articleTitle: Interrupt driven parallel processing
abstract: This article explores the possibilities of new computation architecture. The paper tries to present some modifications in multiprocessor architectures in order to obtain performance increase in computation speed by parallel memory access. In the presented example it is shown how an interrupt can be served skipping the interrupt service routine usual steps.

articleTitle: Application of selected AI models to reconstruction of noise levels at thoroughfare during selected year
abstract: The work briefly presents 3 selected models of noise level at thoroughfare. The models were built by using equivalent sound level data recorded by monitoring station. The methods applied for building the models were Random Forest and regression trees. Next, the obtained models were used for reconstruction of equivalent sound levels for over 60 days for which monitoring station did not record the sound level. Noise level values were reconstructed separately for the following 24-hour sub-intervals: day (6-18), evening (18-22) and night (22-6). The statistical analysis of the sound levels during the whole year, before and after reconstruction, was carried out.

articleTitle: Application of shape memory alloy to vibrating systems
abstract: The paper concerns shape memory alloy (SMA) application to properties control of the vibration isolation systems. These alloys are called “smart” because of their special functions and huge potential usage. Nowadays SMA is used widely in developing new kinds of actuators, clamps and as a material for special tools. Wide range of these applications usually employ one-way shape memory effect and superelasticity. Special properties of SMA are due to thermoelastic phase transformation phenomenon. During these transformations elastic modulus and energy dissipation properties in these smart alloys are changing. This phenomenon of changing SMA properties gets us possibility of applaying them in controlled vibration isolation systems. Such systems could change their properties and could adapt to current changing working conditions. By using SMA we could build smart vibrating systems. In the paper authors show applications of SMA springs to 1-DOF and 2-DOF vibration isolation systems. Moreover, the paper presents results of experimental investigation of 1-DOF and 2-DOF controlled vibration isolation systems conducted in Dynamics and Control of Structures Laboratory of AGH.

articleTitle: Thrust and ignition control of valveless pulse jet engine
abstract: Valveless pulsejets are lightweight, effective in action, low in cost and very simple in assembly. It is excellent to show (for example for students) how this kind of engine works, what parameters we can measure, what type of fuel it is using etc. The main problem is how to control the thrust and preliminary ignition of this engine. The article shows a device to solve this problem. The first part of the article shows mechanical construction made of solenoids and mechanic valves controlling by servomotors creating simple thrust control device. It changes the gas flow. Also, fuel dose can be controlled by a potentiometer on the control panel. What is more, the gas supply can be shut off immediately. The second part of the article shows the ignition system that is created from an ordinary spark plug and electronic silicon board that is using for converting 12V current from the battery into the spark in the spark plug. The last part of the article shows possible uses of the engine and the results of measurements of dependence between fuel flow to creating thrust and dependency between the time of action on full thrust to the temperature of the engine. The article is showing only theoretical approach of the construction, and the operating algorithms which were created on the knowledge acquired during the creation of the psychical prototype showed in the end.

articleTitle: Frequency Filtering of Source Images for LASER Engravers
abstract: This paper deals with image filtering in frequency domain and its effects in area of laser engraving. Current consumer cameras provide high resolution photos which contains dozens megabyte of data. It is not easy task to engrave all the data on wooden materials. Optimal image filtering can decrease production code size up to 30% while preserving quality of the final product. Modular script written in Matlab environment is used for multiple filter types comparison. Effects of frequency filtering to engraving quality and G-Code file size are described.

articleTitle: Modeling and simulation of a parallel quadruped robot
abstract: This paper's focus is on quadruped robot design and kinematics. First, an overall idea is presented focusing on other existing solutions. Next, a custom brushless controller is introduced and a combination of a motor with custom cycloidal gearbox. The idea of actuating the robot's limbs by rods is presented. Forward and inverse kinematics is described as well as different ways of saving the energy in walking robots. In the end, the simulation of the dynamic model is presented in a V-rep program in order to test the position and Euler angles regarding the position of the quadruped's body.

articleTitle: Robust $H_{\infty}$ Controller Design for Active Vibration Suppression with Input Constraints
abstract: This study deals with robust <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> controller design for active vibration suppresion system where the input constraints are taken into consideration in addition to model uncertainties that are present in the system model. Two different approaches are utilized in order to implement the input constraints into the controller design process. The robust <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> controller design algorithms involving input constraints are carried out via linear matrix inequalities and the performance of obtained controllers is illustrated in simulation studies where a two-story structure supplied with an Active-Mass-Damper(AMD) is used.

articleTitle: Surgical tool trajectory optimization in brain tumour resection
abstract: During resection of tumours, which are located inside the brain, normal tissues are also destroyed. It may be reason of permanent brain damage and loss or lesion of some bodily functions. Therefore damages minimization during tumour removing is such important. Knowledge of the tumour localization gives opportunity to planning of path to the tumour and method of its resection. In this paper surgical tool trajectory optimization for brain tumour resection was presented. The computed trajectory is an element of surgical plan. It may be used to automatic brain tumour with usage of the surgical tool, which is mounted on the surgical robot arm. A mathematical description of brain tumour method was described in this paper. A quality indicator was formulated and an optimal trajectory of surgical tool was computed. Results of experiments were analysed and conclusions were presented.

articleTitle: Electric Drive Attack Detection Based on State Observers
abstract: The paper deals with the reasons for the failure of the motor-reducer from the drive and measures to extend its service life. The motor-reducer as an element of the electric drive is widely used in all areas of industry. At the rated load, usually recommended by the manufacturer, the gearbox has its own service life, which is significantly reduced under operating conditions with the maximum permissible load. The attack detection problem is considered as fault detection problem. An observer-based fault detection method for DC-motor with reduction gear is proposed. Simulation results are given.

articleTitle: Measurement System for the Performance Assessment of GNSS Receivers
abstract: With the continuing spread of distributed measurement and control systems (e.g. Cyber-Physical Systems, Industry 4.0) there is an increased need to implement synchronized sampling and actuation over the components of a distributed system. To achieve this goal, the clocks of the system must be synchronized, including the ones doing sampling and actuation. In most cases local synchronization alone is not enough; It is also needed to keep in sync with a global reference time in order, for example, to be able to implement timestamps based on global time and simultaneous sampling across system components that are spatially distributed (operate on different sites). This global reference time mostly means one which is provided by a GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System) service, such as GPS. In these systems, it is the master clock which is responsible for attaining (e.g. via a GNSS receiver) and keeping the global reference time. It can then pass it on in the local communication network, usually using IEEE 1588 (Precision Time Protocol). It follows, that thus, the characteristics of such systems are heavily limited by the precision, accuracy and reliability of the used GNSS receiver. Our paper thus is about the examination of potentially promising GNSS receivers for which we developed a custom measurement system. This includes the design of a test PCB, the writing of a PC data collecting program, the formulation of MATLAB scripts which process the collected data, and the validation of the data collecting system via GNSS receivers simulated by TI evaluation boards. We also conducted measurements with the system on the Quectel L86 GNSS receiver, the results of which are presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Controlling Systems of Conservation Laws - The case of the Open Canals
abstract: Among various real life models for controlled conservation laws, the dynamics of the open canal water flow is such that the nonlinear terms of the partial differential equations cannot be neglected. Starting from a rather complicated model deduced for a quite general case, there are considered some simpler models of the practice, relying on the model of the horizontal prismatic canal with simple cross-section (rectangular, trapezoidal). Basic theory (existence, uniqueness, continuous data dependence) is discussed for small deviations around a steady state. There is also discussed the problem of the invariant sets accounting for fluvialness - some kind of regular behavior of the flow reflected in the partial differential equations and their solutions: absence of cavitation, shock and/or rarefaction waves. Based on the Riemann invariants of the equations there is made the synthesis of the feedback structure for the controllers. These are nonlinear decentralized small gain controllers ensuring linearization and dissipativeness of the boundary conditions in their Riemann invariant forms.

articleTitle: Finding similarities in laser micrometers scanned data using cross-covariance
abstract: This paper demonstrates a signal processing approach designed to overlay data sets measured using two optical micrometers. Two sensors are used in order to measure object's shape, but measured signals are relatively shifted, because it is impossible to mount sensors into the same position. Covariance method are applied to measurement data and the shift between these sets are evaluated.

articleTitle: Mathematical Model of Real CNC Machine
abstract: This paper deals with procedure to compose mathematical model of real CNC laser engraving machine. It uses stiffness, damping ratio and other essential properties of individual machine components to create overall model. Comparison of the model and real machine is described as main performance rate of a model.

articleTitle: Comparison of Conventional and Robust Adaptive Kalman Filters Based Integrated Altimeters
abstract: As a result of the development of modern vehicles, even higher accuracy standards are demanded. As known, Inertial Navigation Systems have an intrinsic increasing error which is the main reason of using integrating navigation systems, where some other sources of measurements are utilized, such as barometric altimeter due to its high accuracy in short times of interval. Using a Robust Adaptive Kalman Filter (RAKF), error measurements are absorbed when a Fault Tolerant Altimeter is implemented. During simulations, in order to test the Nonlinear RAKF algorithm, two kind of measurement fault scenarios are examined; continuous bias and measurement noise increment. Under the light of the results, some recommendations are proposed when integrated altimeters are used.

articleTitle: Aircraft Single-Jet Engine with Hydro-Mechanical Thrust Augmentation System Based on Coolant Injection into the Compressor
abstract: The paper deals with a complex control system of a two-spool single-jet aircraft engine equipped with a coolant injection system into its compressor. The author has defined control system's architecture (consisting of a fuel controller, an exhaust nozzle controller, embedded with a coolant injection controller) and, based on it, has established system's mathematical model. Embedded control system's input and output parameters were established and system's block diagram with transfer functions was built. A study concerning system's quality was performed (embedded system's step response) and some conclusions were presented.

articleTitle: Human Sway Response for the Sine Excitation
abstract: In the case of a man, keeping the balance in a standing position seems obvious and does not require much effort, however, with the appearance of lesions or aging of the body we begin to see how complex the process of controlling the balance is. Maintaining a stable posture is connected above all with the motor control provided by the human nervous system. Equally important is also the unequivocal determination of spatial orientation and consideration of the impact of forces from different sources on the body. The appearance of unpredictable external stimuli that may destabilize the standing position requires an immediate response from the posture stability control system. Analyzing the cases of the first two strategies for maintaining the balance, it can be noticed that both of them, due to their physical nature, resemble inverted pendulum systems and, given some simplifying assumptions, can be modeled as such. The article presents an approach that uses harmonic signal as a disturbance of balance.

articleTitle: The predictive differential-algebraic model for nano-fibrous webs production obtained via electrospinning method
abstract: The electrospun fibrous webs, widely used in many application areas (affinity membranes, drug release, wound dressing, filter media) should not only have the certain functionality, but also adequate fiber size. In this work the predictive differential-algebraic (DAEs) model has been investigated. The model was utilized to study, how the chosen solution-processing parameters may influence the diameter of the polyacrylonitrile (PAN) jet. The presented approach may contribute to the electrospinning process control, as well as to the experimental time/cost reduction.

articleTitle: Determination and measurement of parameters affecting indoor comfort
abstract: There have been numerous publications about how to make smart homes to energy efficient, but few have been born where comfort is the focus. In our article, we determine the parameters and their effects that influence our sense of comfort and present the tools and measurement configurations that can be used to examine these parameters. During this analysis, we are attempting to create a referral system that, during learning, recognizes the habits of the inhabitants of the house and controls the automation system in order to maintain the optimal values. Various procedures are considered for implementing the recommendation system.

articleTitle: Iterative Learning Control for Active Suspension System of a Railway Vehicle
abstract: The paper deals with the automatic control of active force for an active suspension system of railway vehicle. In the first part of the paper, the mathematical model of a simplified active suspension system is derived using the classical Newton laws. The model is represented in the form of a linear first order differential equations system. The control strategy adopted in this paper is Iterative Learning Control (ILC), a control approach intensively used for repetitive processes. In this paper, the repetitive behavior is represented by the body vehicle reaction to track irregularities. From many variants of ILC available in the literature, few simple algorithms were presented: the well-known PD - type algorithms. An heuristic design procedure is implemented for control of a linearized version of the active suspension system. The performances of the proposed control procedure are tested by numerical simulations. The results obtained from the performed simulations show the feasibility of the proposed methods in the case of step-type perturbations.

articleTitle: State-Dependent Fractional-Order PI Control Strategy for a Nonlinear Water Tank System
abstract: The paper presents a control strategy based on variable-order fractional PI controller.
