The control strategy is a state-dependent piecewise constant-order optimization problem, that divides the variation of the state variable into arbitrary intervals and selects different fractional PI orders obtained via constrained numerical minimization in order to best suit the dynamics of the process. Various definitions of order switching, i.e. A-,B-,D- and E -type are investigated. Numerical experiments on identified model of the water tank system are conducted. Results obtained during numerical experiments are then implemented on real physical object - CE105MV Coupled Tanks system. Authors compare obtained results both from numerical and experimental tests with other popular control strategies in respect of outcome but also critical view on complexity of implementation.

articleTitle: Operational properties of vibratory conveyors of the anti-resonance type
abstract: This article is devoted to the analysis of the operating properties of vibratory conveyors, which principle of operations is based on the dynamic elimination effect of the Frahm [1]. These conveyors, according to the data provided by their manufacturers, have several advantages, including higher amplitudes of vibrations at the same drive and extremely low dynamic forces transmitted to the foundation. In the work, a simulation model of such a conveyor loaded with a feed was made and tests of transport efficiency and forces transmitted to the foundation in stationary states and during start-up periods were performed. The numerical simulations carried out concerned various mass ratios constituting the analyzed mechanical system.

articleTitle: Comparison of Microstrip Patch Antennas with Different Materials Operating on 2.46GHz for FSO/RF Hybrid System
abstract: The requirements on the communication systems grow exponentially with number of users. Network providers must react to this trend and find the new way to increase the availability of the services. The majority of the current communication systems were improved by the process of optimization. Some network elements were replaced by adequate replacement. The standard fiber optical communication networks were also modified over the time of use. Free Space Optics (FSO) system is an innovative concept of communication system which should directly replace standard fiber optical systems. The signal transmission in FSO system is based on free propagation through the atmosphere. The optical signal is sensitive to inhomogeneities in the atmosphere. To ensure the availability of 99.999% we developed the backup radio-frequency (RF) link. This backup link is based on microwave transmission. In this paper, the design of patch antenna made out of three different materials (FR04, RO4000 and RT6002) is presented. Because each of the proposed material is characterized by different value of relative permittivity, which affects the performance of antenna, we provide the comparative analysis of electromagnetic compatibility in FEKO software.

articleTitle: Storage kind recognition of truck's timber load
abstract: Every truck heading into the paper mill of company MONDI, Slovakia have to be checked if storage of its timber load meets all safety rules. Each truck is scanned by a group of 2D scanners. Then the evaluation of timber load is done by software with use of the data received from the scanners. Checking software is universal for every kind of storage of timber loads. This article deals with a problem of recognition a kind of storage of timber load on a semi-trailer. The image recognition is done with use of data recorded by a set of cameras situated with its view on the driveway. By detecting a type of storage, it is possible to evaluate the safety check for a specific type of storage with better result than the universal check.

articleTitle: Robust gain scheduled PI-D controller design for descriptor system
abstract: A new approach of gain scheduled PI-D controller design for descriptor system is presented in the proposed paper. The proposed method in the frame of H2 with quadratic criterion ( Q, S, R) ensures robust properties of the closed-loop descriptor system and parameter dependent quadratic stability. The obtained method to robust admissibility analysis of descriptor system with time varying both the uncertain parameters of polytopic systems and gain scheduled variable is expressed in the form of strict LMI. For the D-part of PI-D gain scheduled controller the designer could use any or all outputs of the descriptor system. The designed example exhibits the quality of proposed method.

articleTitle: Comparison of a saturation flow method and an expert system to optimise traffic crossroads control
abstract: In this paper, we will focus on comparing the two methods for optimisation of intersection control. The first method is a saturation flow method, the second method is an expert system that divides the time for each vehicle a given crossing direction based on expert knowledge. For both methods, simulations are created based on real data of a selected crossroad in the city of Ostrava. Based on these simulations, the methods are compared. Subsequently, the comparison is evaluated together with a description of the advantages and disadvantages of the individual methods. The comparison is provided based on real traffic data of a selected crossroad in the city of Ostrava.

articleTitle: Application of evolutionary algorithms to analysis the possibilities of solar energy use
abstract: This publication presents the application of evolutionary algorithms to the analysis of the possibilities of solar energy use. The evolutionary method was discussed, the influence of different values of evolutionary algorithm coefficients on the final result of the calculations was examined. An evolutionary method was used to calculate the dependence of solar radiation no a presence of impurities in the air. The values of solar radiation, PM2.5, PM10, and cloud cover were measured over a period of several months each time at noon in the selected location. The influence of the number of crossover and mutation rate on the result of the algorithm was investigated. The Matlab / Simulink software was used for calculations.

articleTitle: The Welding Current and Voltage Smart Sensor
abstract: This paper describes a procedure of development and testing of a High-speed Current Sensing System (HSCSS). Introduced sensor is based on current transducer where measurement is based on the Hall-effect principle. Sensor is also equipped with precise voltage measurement system. The measurement and data processing are accomplished by the ARM based processor unit. The HSCSS output for communication and data transfer is based on Ethernet line.

articleTitle: Fast Approximate Algorithm for Robust Emergency System Design
abstract: This contribution is aimed at advanced rescue system designing. Since the modelled decisions are strategic and often have a long-term impact on accessibility and effectiveness of service providing, several aspects should be taken into account when a integer-programming model of the problem is created. One of them consists in system robustness that means its resistance to randomly occurring failures in the associated transportation network, which is used by ambulance vehicles when delivering rescue service to system users. To incorporate system robustness into the particular integer-programming model, a finite set of failure scenarios is usually formed. Then, the optimal robust rescue system design can be obtained by minimization of the highest detrimental impact of the individual scenarios. A simple rescue system design can be modelled as a weighted p-median problem. While a weighted p-median problem is easily solvable, the robust system design often causes computational difficulties due to the model size and its complicated structure. Therefore, the main goal of this contribution is to develop a fast algorithm for robust rescue system design, which enables to obtain a good approximate solution of the original problem in a short time. The theoretical explanation is here accompanied by a computational study.

articleTitle: Self-tuning of a Kalman Filter Applied in a DC Drive and in a Kalman-based Sensor
abstract: Kalman filters (KFs) are used in many different areas of application that require a solution to discrete-data linear filtering problems. Especially in the field of electric controls KFs represent a very used approach and an integral part of many states of the art of electric controls. However, the practical implementation of the KF often presents difficulties due to the challenging task of getting a good estimate of the covariance of the process noise represented by matrix Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub> and of the covariance of the measurement noise represented by matrix R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub>. A fitting and simultaneous choice of the matrices Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub> and R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub> based on a feedback loop within the KF realised by the filter samples can lead to a stable-operating filter after a reasonable amount of iterations. In this paper an approach to apply a feedback loop enabling dynamic values Q<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub> and R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sub> is presented. This approach will be applied in a simulation using Matlab/Simulink.

articleTitle: Transmultiplexing as a Method of Protecting Digital Data Against Unauthorized Reading, in IoT Systems in Particular
abstract: Transmultiplexing is a method which combines many independent digital signals into a single complex signal transmitted by a single communication channel. Properly designed, it provides perfect reconstruction of source signals from a complex signal. The data integrity is guaranteed by a set of synthesis and analysis filters banks with integer elements. Filters banks with only `zeros' and `ones' ensure data integrity with minimal computing power. This solution is advantageous for simple IoT systems with many sensors and 8-bit microcontrollers. The paper contains selected examples of filter banks fulfilling a perfect reconstruction for a 4-input and an 8-input transmitter with only `zeros' and `ones' elements. The experimental system with digital sensors (temperature) verify the method of transmultiplexing. The results of attempts to read the proper temperature value from a composite signal sample haves been provided.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Algorithm for the EEG Signal Evaluation
abstract: The aim of the present paper is to propose an alternative technique based on the fuzzy methodology to investigate the dimensional complexity of biomedical signals generated by BCI. The signal identification is based on vectorial multifractal analyse that is mathematically formalized by the spectrum singularities of Hölder exponents evaluated on the interval [0, T]. A fuzzy technique is used to calculate the Hölder exponents of the signal. The Husdorff parameters are evaluated by several techniques: averaging, norm, Center of Gravity Method and spectral estimation. A Type-2 Fuzzy Set method is used to classificate and sorte the signals. Numerical results of the propsed techniques are discussed.

articleTitle: Web tool for creating 3D visualizations with focus on real-time direct manipulation of mathematical objects' attributes
abstract: In this paper we describe a web-based tool for creating and publishing interactive presentations with 2D and 3D visualizations of mathematical objects. It provides ways for enhancing students ability to understand mathematical concepts by means of direct manipulation of functions attributes. Our prototype is realized using Javascript and WebGL and consists of some solved exercises which represent a learning unit. It offers an innovative look at one of possible ways of preparing better teaching material.

articleTitle: PID controller for velocity control and skid prevention for a six-wheeled rover
abstract: Mars rover should be able to maintain a constant speed while running, regardless of the terrain formation and surface's state. This article presents the use of a PID controller when controlling DC motors in a rover in order to obtain a constant angular velocity of each wheel. The rover was equipped with six hub wheels, each fitted with a DC motor including an encoder. The rocker-bogie suspension system presents a challenge when it comes to controlling the robot's traverse conditions. The drive system consists of the STM32 microcontroller controlling high-power motor diver of each engine. The implemented software receives a signal about the current change of position in the encoder, and on its basis the error to which our regulator is to respond is determined. After simulation and in-situ tests, the controller was developed based on carried out observation. Through the fine-tuning process of the regulator's output, we were able to achieve a calm ride at a constant speed on even in the most challenging terrain, as well as maintaining the position of the robot on steep hills.

articleTitle: Computation of Fair Crew Schedules in Regular Bus Transport
abstract: Day shifts of vehicles and corresponding drivers are closely associated in Slovak and Czech conditions. This means that such a running board of a bus can be serviced only with one or two subsequent drivers. Therefore running boards of vehicles are also driver shifts at the same time and that's why they have to comply to all safety rules required by law and also to Labour Code working conditions. However, it is necessary to follow other rules when creating schedules. One of them is a requirement for uniform workload for drivers. Too short shifts, long shifts with many and long waiting times and little driving could be very poorly paid and therefore dismissed by majority of drivers. If the schedules for the individual drivers were too different, some drivers would be too dissatisfied. We present here two algorithms for creating a bus schedule which is fair from the point of view of drivers. The problem of creating a schedule can be formulated by two ways - as a problem of bivalent linear programming, and as a problem discrete optimization based on manyfold combinations of heads and tails, resp. of bodies and fixed heads and tails of starting bus schedule.

articleTitle: Examination of power loss and voltage drop of a solar panel as a function of environmental factors
abstract: This electronic document presents the voltage drop of a solar panel as a function of environmental factors. Voltage and power production of a solar panel depends heavily on the amount of irradiation which reaches the surface of the panel. The ideal output of a photovoltaic module is determined by many factors. Environmental factors directly affect the voltage and power production, pollutants on the surface, for example, can create shadow effect. Why is this important - one may ask. Energy production and efficiency of the photovoltaic module are experimentally investigated with different types of contaminations, such as dust, leaves or cement. Measurements are executed with different contaminated areas and different amounts of pollution. Power production and the type of contamination show a certain correlation. It is possible to determine how the voltage and power production drop depend on the surface contaminants.

articleTitle: Grobman-Hartman Theorem for Control Systems containing parameter uncertainties
abstract: The Grobman-Hartman theorem makes the investigation of differential equations easy in a neighbor of an equilibrium point. When nonlinear systems are studied, parameters are considered as constant, but in case of control systems, the system usually contains parameter uncertainties which can result in differences with respect to the expected behavior. We give a version of the Grobman-Hartman theorem for control systems containing parameter uncertainties.

articleTitle: Research of magnetic system applied in autonomous MegaSumo robots
abstract: Research of magnetic system applied in autonomous MegaSumo robots is an important issue in the best adaptation of a fighting robot. Only this type of robots (dimensions 200×200 mm, weight up to 3000g) are obliged to use it. It is caused by the driving of robots on the metal rings (dohyo). To get the best movement characteristics, magnets are attached to the robot's floor. The quantity of magnets results in high or low traction during the fight. High magnetising power does not allow the opponent to get under the robot and push it out of the ring. In the article, simulation research was carried out on three different magnetic systems that can be used in a robot. After the simulations, each system was built in reality. In order to check the actual attractive forces of the system, tests were carried out on the strength machine. This allowed comparing the results from simulations and real tests. The best layout was used in the sumo robot. It had the greatest strength of attraction for a metal dohyo.

articleTitle: On demand vison-based indoor localization
abstract: Many indoor localization systems are based on earth-magnetic or radio field strength fingerprinting which is considering its low computing power requirement is very well-suited method for mobile phone applications. However, certain parts of navigation areas might not cover with any radio signal which makes the localization very difficult and imprecise. In this case the mobile phone camera can be used as a temporary localization sensor. Since the mobile phone camera is usually not stereo or depth sensing camera and since the image processing capabilities of the mobile phone is limited, a specific algorithm needs to be developed. The algorithm is expected to work without using any special markers, using only existing features of the surrounding environment, recognizing them, using a database to lookup their position and using a Perspective-n-Point algorithm to determine the user's relative position. The markers can be any specific feature of the building or any logo, sign or anything visually specific to the given location. This article summarizes the development, tuning and testing of a mobile phone application using marker-less vision-based localization algorithm..

articleTitle: Iterative Learning Control for a Rotary Flexible Joint Experiment
abstract: This paper deals with the Iterative Learning Control (ILC) of a Flexible Joint Experiment. The paper presents a short overview of the field of Iterative Learning Control and some basic ILC strategies (P - type and D - type) are highlighted. The design of ILC for linear systems is briefly presented. The ILC is implemented on a Flexible Joint experiment, working in repetitive manner, where the control goal is the trajectory tracking. Even the Flexible Joint is a nonlinear system, in order to tune the controller parameters a linear model is derived. The controller performances are evaluated using a real plant experiment. The main experimental results are presented and the performance of the control system is analyzed.

articleTitle: Distortions Correction Plants in Textile Industry. Nonlinear Modelling and Control
abstract: In the textile industry, the operation of textile plants is hindered by some defects, derivations or distortions in the weaving process of the fabric. Related to these distortion corrections, one of the critical operations is the so-called recovery operation (orthogonalization) of fabrics resulting from the loom. The orthogonalization plants realize a certain angle between warp threads and weft yarns of fabrics. In this paper we develop a mathematical model of the curvature correction and a nonlinear control structure for the entire orthogonalization process. Adaptation is necessary due to the change in the quality of the fabric and its driving velocity. Thus, a nonlinear adaptive and structure variable control is proposed. Several numerical simulations illustrate the behaviour of the proposed control structure.

articleTitle: A Disturbance Observer-Based Control of Drilling Vibrations
abstract: This paper presents two control strategies to suppress the unwanted torsional vibrations occurring in a drill string system. The control scheme uses a disturbance estimation procedure, which ensures the rejection of this uncertainness, allowing the robustness improvement of closed loop system. A constrained predictive command obtained by solving a minimization problem and a linearized control are derived, and validation results are presented to prove the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: The concept of POSTURON braces for patients with a damaged labyrinth
abstract: The objective of the article is to present posturographic apparatus called POSTURON built on the shape of braces with IMU sensors, which in combination with a microprocessor and a program to process these data, allow assessing the patient's current state of balance and if necessary help him in its correction through vibrational signals. The primary assumption is to speed up the recovery of patients with imbalances and to increase the mobility of people with a permanently damaged balance apparatus and create a device that registers and corrects the posture also during outpatient rehabilitation and providing protection against falling. The device should be very burdensome for the patient, i.e., be light and comfortable. In order to increase the mental comfort of the examined apparatus, it should be less visible. Healthy persons, as well as those with imbalances, were recruited for the study. Based on the results obtained, we assessed the impact of the device on the quality of the exercises performed.

articleTitle: Minimization of vibrations during milling of flexible structures using mechatronic design techniques
abstract: The paper presents an innovative effective method of minimizing vibrations during milling of flexible structures, using a new vibration suppression method based on a workpiece holder with adjustable support stiffness. The proposed method is rooted in mechatronic design techniques, which can become a standard procedure for optimizing the milling process.

articleTitle: Cascade classifier as a tool for quick camera calibration
abstract: The mobile robotics development is very rapid nowadays. In the interest of companies and institutions is to transfer more and more task for mobile robots. The conversion from one application to other even similar is often associated with changes in hardware. The authors have performed a study witch effects possibility to significantly reduce the time of computer vision system calibration. The following paper presents multiple cameras calibration process for mobile robotics applications. The selection of applicable marker for cascade classifier training is described. Then the calibration of various cameras is shown. To perform this task the authors used application created by them especially for this. Results with emphasis for calibration errors are one of the most important parts of the paper. In the end, there are conclusions and prediction for further development and usage of this application.

articleTitle: Evaluation of temperature changes of a loaded DC motor in autonomous mobile robots
abstract: In this paper, the analysis of the temperature changes of a loaded DC motor is presented. The motor is being used in autonomous robots in MegaSumo category. The research object was Maxon Motor RE40 150W, which is a frequent choice of autonomous mobile robots' constructors. High power, small size, simplicity and precision of control are primary factors that make these motors popular. This study aimed to develop a protection scheme of MegaSumo robot's power components, battery, motors, and their drivers through estimation of safe work time of a loaded motor in the robot activity time based on instantaneous power loss in the motor. In order to evaluate the thermal response of the motor's internal components, a mathematical model was created basing on both experimental and motor manufacturers data. The research based on a model was carried out in Matlab/Simulink software suite.

articleTitle: Modelling and Simulation of Autonomous Systems with Voltage Inverters, Output Filters and Asynchronous Motors
abstract: This paper presents a new model of control principle for autonomous systems based on asynchronous motors fed by static power converters. All the coefficients required for control are determined by Fourier analysis of the output voltage waveform. The resulting dynamic system model is able to accurately predict the system response. The inverters are used for many modern autonomous systems where the direct current voltage sources, such as lithium-ion batteries, solar panels, or combustion cells, have to be transformed so that the devices can run fed from an alternating current source of variable voltage and frequency. The new methods proposed are verified by simulation, by the analysis of the diagrams of stator voltage, stator current, rotor speed and electromagnetic torque, and by the dynamic behaviour of a real experimental model. A Fourier analysis model identification approach and the reducing of harmonics determine the optimum performances in terms of losses, heat and noise of the induction motor, system or vehicle.

articleTitle: Shock Response Spectrum Calculation from Container Placing
abstract: This paper deals with using shock response spectrum for container placing optimization. Two types of laying pads under container are used and its impact to container substructures is observed. Shock response spectrum is calculated with using Signal Analyser software from signal measured with accelerometers during container placing. The resulted spectrum for both pads is compared.

articleTitle: An Improved Numerical Method for the Simulation of Nonlinear Systems
abstract: Because the models that arise from the bioindustry are highly nonlinear, in order to simulate them we propose an adaptive PID control of step-size, where the variation of the step-size is proportional to the error criterion and a digital filter is used in order to smoothen up the step-size variation. The present paper compares this numerical method with a wide selection of numerical methods that can be used in order to simulate the evolution of the systems. Although the application is designed with the purpose of simulating the evolution of mathematical models that arise from the food processing industry, it can also be used for models that come from other areas of the industry. The proposed numerical method is tested and validated by using some nonlinear models of classical systems such as Lorenz and Van der Pol, but also nonlinear models of bioprocesses.

articleTitle: The algorithm for evaluation of data for calibration of the triangulation laser scanner
abstract: The paper describes an algorithm that is part of the methodology for calibrating single point triangulation 2D scanners with tilting mirrors. This system is affected by the nonlinearity given by errors of triangulation range-finder, optics and tilting mechanism. They are caused, for example, by eccentric placement of mirrors to the axis of tilting, mirror unevenness or deviation in the sensor location. Another type of error occurs when incorrect measuring of the tilt angle of mirrors and either incorrect definition of the function that describe the shape of the tilt cam, or errors caused by the dynamic forces during movement. Methodology is designed to analyze data from repeated measurements of the reference objects in different positions, statistically evaluate points, remove noise and count corrections for image obtained by a known shape of test object, even though the position of object is not precisely measured.

articleTitle: Differential filters in an adaptive control system
abstract: This article presents an algorithm for adaptive control of a plotter head. It discusses the use of differential filters in control algorithms. The filters are designed to determine the derivatives of the input signal and eliminate measurement and quantization noise. The primary purpose of the study was to employ the differential filters in a real-time control algorithm, which requires appropriate derivatives. The experiments were conducted on a test stand with a plotter equipped with an electric drive acting as the plant to be controlled.

articleTitle: An Advanced Method of Recognizing the State of the Technological Process in Technical Diagnostics
abstract: Technical diagnostics is an independent science field. It deals with non-destructive methods and means to determine the status of the object or process. It uses knowledge based on the heuristic principle and mathematical models of diagnosed objects. Reliability of the technical equipment is conditional upon monitoring the technical condition of the object and the ongoing processes. In technical diagnostics, beside to standard signal processing methods, they are increasingly applied in addition to advanced signal analysis methods, based on artificial intelligence, neural networks, fuzzy logic, and expert systems. Of great importance in this area is the system approach. This paper discusses the possibilities and uses of the vector quantization method. For the method, the state space of the system or metric space is important. The method makes it possible to recognize the state closest to it from the previously defined possible states by measuring the appropriate set of state quantities of the technical device. Recognized equipment status may be linked to the corresponding maintenance, efficient control, and safety operations. The proposed method is based on the continuous evaluation of the measured variables classified into the appropriate class.

articleTitle: Uncertainty Budget for Calibration of Platinum Resistance Thermometer
abstract: The aim of this article is to describe the problem of determining measurement uncertainties in the temperature calibration, especially the calibration of the platinum resistance thermometer. Two calibration methods can be used - comparison calibration method or calibration in defined temperature points in the appropriate temperature scale. This paper describes a first calibration method that is based on comparing the value from a calibrated temperature sensor to a temperature value measured by a reference temperature sensor (standard). The uncertainty budget for platinum resistance thermometer and the calibration system is given here.

articleTitle: A new procedure for solving differential-algebraic equations
abstract: In this article a new algorithm for solving differential-algebraic equations (DAEs) was presented. The designed procedure was based on variability constraints and reduced model of considered system equations, characterized by constant dynamics and linearized system of algebraic equations. A multiple shooting approach was applied to divide an independent variable range into assumed number of subintervals. This approach resulted in nonlinear optimization task (NLP) with pointwise-continuous constraints. Therefore, the presented procedure was based on the efficient nonlinear optimization algorithm. Finally, some implementation issues were discussed. The effectiveness of the presented methodology was presented on a process design task subject to a nonlinear differential-algebraic model of a chemical reactor.

articleTitle: System for Automating the Search for Coloured Cells in Images
abstract: The strategy of Industry 4.0 brings numerous tasks for automating activities until now performed by humans. Those activities mainly include tasks based on image analysis and computer vision. Our workplace deals with many tasks of this type. The paper presents results of a specific task - automating the search for coloured cells in images. The task takes its grounds from cooperation in biochemical research projects. Such research requires analysing a huge amount of cell samples, some of which are variously coloured in order to determine their ratio on the total number of cells. This analysis has been done by manual counting so far, which is very time-consuming and whose accuracy has not been verified. Basic used algorithms are image segmentation, colour thresholding, and active contour analysis. Several methods have been tested with achieved detection accuracy of 414 cells out of 470. Further solution will deal with the division of the remaining cells. This process will take advantage of an artificial intelligence method and machine learning, most likely a neural network.

articleTitle: Detection Of The Road Defects In The Tunnel Area
abstract: This article presents research results in the area of 3D scanning of the tunnel roadway surface and its surroundings. Then it describes analysis of the obtained models with respect to the safety of the road traffic inside tunnel. Presented method allows to create and analyze 3D model of the roadway surface. From the analysis of the model, it is possible to determine the degradation degree of the roadway and provide basic info required for its repair. Method has been verified by several testing analyses.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation on an energy storage in a piezoelectric harvester for a rotating shaft
abstract: An experimental investigation on an energy storage in a piezoelectric energy harvester is a subject of article The piezoelectric energy harvester consisted of Macro Fiber Composite patch, Graetz Bridge and capacitor. Macro Fiber Composite patch was direct glued on a rotating shaft surface, which was a source of mechanical energy. Such structure of energy harvester enabled the obtaining of linear increase of voltage values which were generated by the harvester. Laboratory experiments contained measurements of voltage across a capacitors, which are the storage device in energy harvesting circuit. On the basis of laboratory results and discussion it noticed that an electric power, which is delivered from a piezoelectric material to a capacitor in the energy harvesting circuit, is dependent on the voltage across this capacitor for constant maximal stress values and constant frequency of value change of stress in a piezoelectric material.

articleTitle: Discrete Sliding-Mode Control of Remote Peer in MPTCP Streaming Applications
abstract: Most of the network-related applications transfer data using the TCP protocol. While TCP has not been designed to handle real-time or multimedia streams, the ubiquitous security devices and administrative restrictions force to use it also in such cases. Usually, it is expected to transfer data as fast as possible. In many classes of applications, however, the streams can be blocked by the network, as well as by the receiver application. Then, a large buffer at the receiver side, or expensive preferences in the network administration, need to be implemented to avert the deterioration of user experience. Instead, the recently developed multi-path variant of TCP (MPTCP) can be applied. Nevertheless, the algorithms managing MPTCP transmission have not been developed to govern the application-restricted streams. In the paper, a discrete sliding-mode paradigm has been chosen for the design of a data flow controller. It deals with simultaneous transmission of data via paths with diverse parameters, e.g., different throughput and delays. The algorithm establishes a feasible (non-negative and bounded) input signal. Executed desirably at the sender side, it prevents both exhausting and overflowing the receiver buffer despite uncertain networking conditions. The properties of the designed control system are analyzed formally and illustrated by numerical tests.

articleTitle: Tuning of the non-linear fractional-order controller
abstract: This paper deals with an optimal tuning of the non-linear fractional-order controller parameters. An optimization algorithm of the tuning method for such kind of the 6 degrees of freedom controller is presented. Suggested tuning technique is based on the modified Nelder-Mead optimization algorithm applied to control loop for well defined cost function. On illustrative example the proposed novel methodology is demonstrated.

articleTitle: A modified micro-genetic algorithm for robust emergency system designing
abstract: We study a robust emergency system in a transport network where it is necessary to solve a problem of finding p service centers for randomly emergency demands in nodes. The objective of our problem is to minimize the upper bound of partial object functions for given number of detrimental scenarios. Transport network is modelled in a matrix form i.e elements of the matrix are response times from a potential service center to a location of an user. Such matrix is given for every detrimental scenario. At last every location is given a number of shared users. We present modified micro-genetic algorithm on the instance of transport network of Slovak Republic. We verify it in selected regions of network via comparing it to known exact solutions. We also seek an approximate solution for a total network.

articleTitle: Creating of detrimental scenarios for a robust rescue system
abstract: The rescue system is represented by few service centers (fire and rescue stations) and many customers (probable locations of first aid or fire), which are some nodes of a transportation network. Service centers were located so that each customer was served from his associated center with respect to the time limit. The unlikely events (excessive snow, black ice, accidents, traffic jams and so on) are increasing the traveling time between the customers and associated centers. In this article we study structure of transport network. We want to find some critical ways (arcs in directed graph) which makes the current (specified) location of centers unusable. Several failures will be modeled by increasing the traveling time simultaneously on multiple ways. This will result not only to an increase of the traveling time between customer and his center, but also to change the route or even change the associated center. An algorithm to find critical ways in transport network for specified service centers locations, based on Paluchs K-shortest path algorithm, will be presented.

articleTitle: Automatic Test Generator for Analytic Geometry
abstract: The basic part of higher education is examination. Modern education implement ICT tools for generate test. In this paper, we propose an automatic test generator based on worksheet generator for analytic geometry. This Automatic test generator is designed for our basic undergraduate course Mathematics 2 at the Faculty of Mining, Ecology, Process Control and Geotechnologies, Technical University of Košice. We focus on the analysis and design of analytic geometry examples and implementation of automatic test generator.

articleTitle: Wireless control system for an intelligent home
abstract: This paper defines the concept of a new home-based solution for the future that has high performance intelligent systems to control more critical parameters such as humidity, temperature, lighting, door and window state, house energy consumption and many other features. The paper includes essential issues related to the design and implementation of an inexpensive and secure home security system for the general users. A wireless sensor network based on ESP8266, Raspberry Pi3 and a series of open source software packages introduces a very attractive feature in scalability, cost, compactness, ease of maintenance, ease of deployment and ease of customization of the entire system control. The security level is increased due to the use of Raspberry Pi3 control, which has built-in capabilities, sends SMS to the user, and is easily connected to other external devices.

articleTitle: Discrete Time Trajectory Following Sliding Mode Control Strategy
abstract: This paper deals with the problem of discrete time sliding mode control with an external trajectory generator. We consider a disturbed discrete time dynamical system and present a new reference trajectory based sliding mode control strategy. We adopt the nonswitching type definition of the quasi-sliding mode and, following the main stream of research on the topic, we use the reaching law approach to design the control. We propose generating the desired trajectory of the system externally, using a new nonswitching type reaching law. Then, we define a new desired trajectory following reaching law for the disturbed plant. We demonstrate that the trajectory following reaching law limits the impact of external disturbances and model uncertainties on the system to one step, whereas in the existing control methods the performance of the system is influenced by all disturbance values from the beginning of the control process. Therefore, our control strategy guarantees a reduction of the width of the ultimate band and increases the system's robustness. The results of our study are verified with a simulation example.

articleTitle: Cheap Automated Guided Vehicles - concept and experiments
abstract: The robotic platforms used for ensure the transfer of the semi-finished product within a company are proven to be useful compared to conventional conveyor systems through flexibility, reliability, fast maintenance with a much higher degree of reservation than other systems, but especially through the possibility of fast reconfigurability in line with the current market economy requirements. The present paper addresses this reality in conjunction with a real situation identified within a company, going through all the specific stages, from the concept to the physical implementation of the prototype. Successfully experienced solution by the authors has focused not only on satisfying the requirements imposed by the concept, but also to identifying cheap, easy-to-buy components by any company. Thus, certain components of a usual Segways and control subsystem that can be quickly purchased through on-line commerce (shields and controllers from the Arduino family) are used. At the end of the article, the conclusions outlined propose potential beneficiaries a number of possibilities to extend the proposed concept, along with a procedure for selecting the main components that are part of the CAGY.

articleTitle: Traffic Regulation Velocity Obstacles method
abstract: The goal of this paper is to show a new concept of the reactive motion planning algorithms for mobile robots in dynamic environment using the main rules of the Traffic Regulation. At the presented solution the algorithm uses the velocity vectors and positions of the obstacles and the robot so the Velocity Obstacles (VO) method seems to be a good choice as a basis for the motion planning. As an assumption the obstacles do not change their velocities during the sampling time. In that case the method can plan evasive maneuvers between the robot and the obstacles. In this work, a new motion planning method is introduced that plans the velocities and the path for the mobile robot using the basic Traffic Regulations. The solution method was extended with emergency vehicles that changes the use of the Traffic Regulations during the motion planning. This method provides an appropriate solution also if there are more obstacles in the workspace. The results of the motion of the obstacles and the robot were tested in simulations.

articleTitle: Longitudinal Vibration Of the Linear Piezo Actuators
abstract: The paper deals with the mathematical modeling longitudinal vibrations of the linear piezo actuators. The theory of the vibration of continuous structures is applied for modeling a stacked piezo actuator, which is considered as a continuous cantilever beam. The model has a form of a partial differential equation, which is solved with the use of the method of separation of variables (Fourier method). The calculation of the natural frequencies of the piezo actuator and the analysis of the effect of the loading mass on these frequencies is the main result of the paper.

articleTitle: Range Sensor-based Occupancy Grid Mapping with Signatures
abstract: Recently autonomous navigation technologies have received huge attention in many fields, such as autonomous driving or mobile robotics. Simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) [1] is a key problem in this field and the current paper targets the mapping part of it. Mapping means to construct accurate static or even dynamic representation of the observable environment. There are of course solutions for range sensor-based mapping, but the current paper proposes a new approach, which involves signatures. Signature is a mathematical data representation, which handles well uncertainty in complex systems.

articleTitle: Wheelchair control by head motion using a noncontact method in relation to the pacient
abstract: As the EU population is getting older, the number of Europeans with disabilities is rising significantly. Among them, a consistent percentage is represented by persons with severe mobility impairment, making them dependent of wheelchairs. This paper proposes a human - wheelchair command interface based on head movement tracking. The head movements are tracked using an artificial vision-based system. The wheelchair user can select between two control modes - in a first control mode, simple commands (as left, right, forward, stop) are given; in the second control mode, the wheelchair movements are correlated with both amplitude and speed of head movement. For the both control modes, the wheelchair movement commands are assisted by a 3D cartography analysis system, having the role to prevent the collision with near-by obstacles.

articleTitle: Application of Support Vector Regression for Data-Driven Modeling of Melt Temperature and Carbon Content in LD Converter
abstract: Oxygen steel making process is a method of primary steelmaking in which carbon-rich molten pig iron is made into steel. Blowing oxygen through molten pig iron lowers the carbon content of the alloy and changes it into low-carbon steel. The temperature of melt inside the LD converter cannot be continually measured directly by thermocouples due to the destructive high temperature. Therefore, methods for estimating temperature using the model are developed. This paper presents a proposal for a non-contact soft-sensing based on the support vector regression (SVR). The proposed machine learning model can predict melt temperature and carbon content in the melt continually during steelmaking. The data-driven model is based on a large number of direct measurements at the start and end points of the melt. It was found that the polynomial kernel used in SVR gives more often better qualitative and quantitative prediction results. Achieved results have shown that this approach may be a potential alternative to traditional metallurgical models.

articleTitle: Mathematical Modelling and Control for an Activated Sludge Process in a Wastewater Treatment Plant
abstract: The paper addresses the modelling and the design of an adaptive control structure for an aerobic fermentation process under the realistic assumption that some state variables are unmeasurable, the reaction kinetics are incompletely known and time-varying and the influent flow rate has very large variations. More exactly, the studied process is a wastewater biological treatment process, with activated sludge, carried out in a continuous perfectly mixed bioreactor implemented in the Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) Făcăi, Craiova, Romania. The behaviour and performance of control algorithms are evaluated by several numerical simulations and are compared with the real outputs of the mentioned plant. The aim of this study is to improve the plant performance by implementation of the proposed control algorithms.

articleTitle: Real-World Robotic Competitions for Radiological and Nuclear Inspection Tasks
abstract: Lessons learned from the Chernobyl and Fukushima disasters and from decommissioning of old nuclear facilities show that robots have certain advantages in this field. However, especially in situations with radiological and nuclear (RN) threats robotic systems have been of very limited practical use so far. This is mainly due to the severe technical difficulties and the lack of testing possibilities for such scenarios. But there is also a limited interest of the scientific community. One possible means to tackle these problems is through robotic trials and competitions. The paper motivates this approach and presents advantages and possible drawbacks. Afterwards, some of the few already established competitions with radiological and nuclear tasks and scenarios are described. For each of these events a detailed insight into the setting and the tasks, the obtained results, and the future way ahead is presented.

articleTitle: Control of an activated sludge wastewater treatment process based on a Calibrated and modified BSM1 Model
abstract: This paper presents process modeling and dissolved oxygen concentration control loop design for an intermittently operated municipal wastewater treatment plant with the goal to reduce the operational costs and further improve effluent quality. A modified Benchmark Simulation Model No.1 (BSM1) developed according to a medium municipal wastewater treatment plant of 4500 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>/day capacity was used as a working scenario. The model was calibrated and validated based on data collected from the real plant. Calibration was performed by varying the kinetic parameters of the model to match the simulation results to experimental data. The model validation was achieved by using several common performance indexes described in the literature. A dissolved oxygen concentration control strategy was designed and tested on the calibrated model. The results indicate a considerable energy saving compared to the initial plant control system.

articleTitle: Fast Fourier processing and real-time transformation system for a dynamic vibration signal
abstract: Within Industry 4.0 one of the most important aspects is processing speed. In the case of a complex system of vibration signal processing, for the system to be reliable, it takes as little processing time as possible for useful information. This article proposes a parallel implementation of a vibration signal processing system using the National Instruments Compact RIO 9024 system. In today's industrial environments, with engines of all kinds, one of the main problems consist in the vibration problems. This article presents a complete monitoring system for vibration signals analysis in parallel. Some of the main advantages of this proposed monitoring system are the low price, low consumption, but also the fast delivery response according to the level and the proposed processing algorithm. Within the framework of the research activity there are a series of results obtained with the measurement framework in different working scenarios. The problem of monitoring vibration signals is complex because of their dynamics, but within this article a series of optimizations are proposed to make a system as accurate as possible.

articleTitle: Experiments regarding implementation of a virtual training environment for automotive industry
abstract: Training operators for activities ran on automotive manufacturing lines is a long, thorough and laborious process that aims to generate a correct collection of information and actions as well as adequate staff training. Schooling operators has always been costly; therefore, developing an application will facilitate learning the necessary skills. The time until an operator will become productive will be significantly shorter and the exposure to certain risks will also be removed. Learning process can be monitorized for each operator, keeping track of his progress. This allows to estimate completion time of the training and to express an overview on future work activities. At the same time, the operator will acquire skills faster, which normally require long practice and a high level of dexterity. Thus, the authors' proposal is to develop an application for the operators training, within the manufacturing lines, aiming to experiment, in a virtual environment the simulation and the orderly assembly of objects as a stack form. Also, it will be necessary to develop a glove prototype that will have the ability to manipulate and control objects in a virtual environment. The end of this paper will reveal reasons for investing and implementing a new way of teaching, making use of such an application.

articleTitle: Identification of the Wind Turbine Model with MR Damper Based Tuned Vibration Absorber
abstract: The paper concerns laboratory model of a wind turbine tower-nacelle system equipped with magnetorheological (MR) damper based tuned vibration absorber (TVA). The objective of the paper is the identification of the regarded system for the control purposes, i.e. precise representation of the dynamics of the tower-nacelle structure with MR TVA for the assumed model complexity. The laboratory test rig of the considered physical system is referenced. Three stage identification methodology and tests are discussed. The experimental and simulation time and frequency responses are compared. This paper is a second section of a two-part model identification study.

articleTitle: Teaching Hardware Implementation of Neural Networks using High-Level Synthesis in Less Than Four Hours for Engineering Education of Intelligent Embedded Computing
abstract: This paper presents the motivation and design of a mini-course to teach hardware implementation of neural networks using high-level synthesis (HLS) in less than four hours for engineering education of intelligent embedded computing. By standing on the shoulders of giants, the combination of the real-world problem, decoding the process of neural networks hardware design and using HLS as hands-on lab, the students are able to not only pick up the underlying concepts of digital system design naturally but also implement a real working neural networks hardware accelerator in person. Thus, the main contribution of the work is to facilitate the engineering education of hardware design more engaging and practical.

articleTitle: A mechatronic experimental system for control of fluid level in LabVIEW
abstract: A sequential closed-loop control system based on a hybrid P-correction is applied to maintain the desired setpoint level at leakages and to follow a prescribed series of time-varying reference levels. Mathematical models of the two configurations of the investigated hydraulic control system are implemented using LabVIEW virtual instruments. As a result, there are identified approximate characteristics of the system parameters as well as time histories of the process variable converging to reference set-points. Reference input, being introduced to evaluate the effectiveness and robustness of the regulation of level height with periodic intakes of water.

articleTitle: Interaction Between Human and AI Systems - When Automated Systems Move Towards Autonomous
abstract: This paper is inspired by our work on a diploma thesis focused on monitoring the performance of process control assets. Over the years, what makes an organization successful has been a frequently asked question. It is possible to improve its processes, those routines that consists of a set of controlled actions to accomplish a specific goal, depending on individual projects, but it is important to support sustainable principles as they align the organizational activities with clearly defined goals and benchmarks. Key Performance Indicator (KPI) is defined as a measurable value that demonstrates how effectively a process is running and reaching its targets. We would like to demonstrate with an example from industry, on how the methods of process measurements can change depending on the availability of complete, correct and consistent data, enabling training AI algorithms and supporting the idea of creating an augmented expert.

articleTitle: Simulation of a solar power plant
abstract: This electronic document presents the numeric simulation of a solar power plant. Integrating solar power plants into the domestic electricity network raises serious regulatory issues. The voltage level provided by solar power plants can change rapidly, since it depends on environmental factors and on the surface temperature of the solar cells. At extreme temperatures, the provided voltage can exceed the prescribed standard value, therefore an intervention - primarily hysteresis voltage regulation - becomes necessary. The present study describes the effect of a 680.4 kW<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub> solar power plant on the voltage of the power grid as a function of ambient temperature, through simulation results.

articleTitle: Modelling and control of a full vehicle active suspension system
abstract: The work is devoted to the modelling and control of a wheeled vehicle active suspension driven by electrohydraulic actuators. A full suspension model of a SUV type wheeled vehicle was proposed by the authors. In order to formulate the control law of the vehicle suspension, it was necessary to include in the model all elements which have an influence on its dynamic properties. Vertical vibrations as well as pitch and roll was taken into account. In modelling of lateral swaying, torsion bars have been taken into account which are of great importance. For the construction of the active suspension of the wheeled vehicle, the authors used hydraulic cylinders controlled by proportional pressure valves. As a master controller, an optimal control with a quadratic quality indicator was used. Each of the strut suspensions has been equipped with a direct controller whose purpose was to reduce vertical vibrations. Longitudinal and lateral vibrations are reduced by the use of a master controller. Thanks to the use this type of control, it was possible to formulate a quality indicator which takes into account both driving comfort and good vehicle handling. The literature review shows that research of the active suspension control is generally carried out on models reduced to a quarter of a vehicle suspension. The original, 7DOF model of SUV suspension and dynamics equations describing the actuators - which enabled the synthesis of control for the real object - were used in this work.

articleTitle: Multiple Observer with Applications to Landing in Lateral-Directional Plane
abstract: The paper deals with the design of a new full-order multiple observer for Takagi-Sugeno fuzzy systems; the aim is to estimate both the state and the unknown inputs in the case of airplanes' landing in lateral-directional plane. Simplicity, the lack of constraints, as well as the avoidance of the pole placement technique are the strong points of the new observer; also, the effectiveness of the observer is high due to the fact that it is software implemented with commercially available software and because of its important degrees of design freedom and generality. The purpose of the new observer will be both the state vector and the unknown inputs' estimation. For validation, the new algorithm is software implemented for the landing process in lateral-directional plane.

articleTitle: State Constraints in Discrete-time Positive System Control
abstract: The paper solves the problem of state feedback control design for discrete-time positive system. Constraining the system inputs, and exhibit the state variables in an ellipsoidal positive invariant set, the existence of positive feedback control gain matrix is given in terms of the solvability of a set of linear matrix inequalities, guaranteing positive closed-loop structure and stability. Presented numerical examples illustrate practical validity and efficiency of the methodology.

articleTitle: Measurement-control system based on the Cortex-M7 core microcontroller for testing energy harvesting structures
abstract: The paper deals with design, structure, functional testing and application of measurement-control system equipped with 32-bit microcontroller based on ARM Cortex-M7 core. The system enables testing electronic circuits, electric transducers, self-powered vibration reduction systems based on magnetorheological dampers and electromagnetic harvesters. The system includes dedicated extension modules which allow to adapt a number of analog and digital inputs/outputs very easy. The software of the system engineered by the authors is based on FreeRTOS real-time system.

articleTitle: Laboratory measurements and numeric simulation of a solar cell
abstract: This electronic document presents the laboratory measurements and numeric simulation of a solar cell. Many factors determine the efficient operation of a photovoltaic cell, such as the intensity and the spectral composition of illumination. Such parameters are the surface temperature of the solar cell, the intensity and spectral composition of the illumination, ambient temperature, contaminations in the air and on the surface of the cells. Present study is bound to describe the effect of temperature gradient on the amperage and power output of a commercial solar cell through experimental and numerical methods. Said investigations made it possible to better our knowledge about the behavior of a solar cell using constant intensity illumination with and without cooling. After the measurements, we came to the conclusion that by increasing the temperature of the solar cell, the power output will drop. Comparing these results with that of the simulations, we can state that a good tendential similarity was achieved.

articleTitle: Filtering and fingerprint matching methods for Wi-Fi radio map based indoor localization
abstract: Usually the indoor localization methods are using predictor-corrector methods for the precise location determination. The prediction is based on the analysis of the motion of the user, while the correction is based on a radio map-based fingerprinting. There are some application fields where the precision of the predictor-corrector algorithm is sacrificed for the simplicity of sensors and devices. The recent development of the smartwatches they became ideal devices for monitoring elderly people's health conditions together with their indoor location and activity. Since it is not a navigation like application the expected precision and sample rate of the location determination is lower, however the typical sensors configuration of a smartwatch is more limited compared to a mobile phone. Usually the sensors are required for the motion prediction methods are missing, so the common predictor-corrector methods, filters are not applicable for this type of use case. Different algorithms and filtering methods needs to be developed and applied for this application. This article summarizes our approach and results in developing fingerprint only indoor localization application.

articleTitle: Laser Guidance System for Automated Material Distribution in the Industrial Environment
abstract: At present, the primary trend in the industry is to eliminate the human factor involved in routine activities such as the distribution of materials. The presented laser guidance system belongs to the family of the line following systems. The application of this system is particularly useful in indoor environments that do not allow for technological reasons, the implementation of colored or magnetic tracks. The laser guidance system is suitable for transparent linear point-to-point crossing or a sharp, angled trajectory without polynomial turns. The principle is based on a statically positioned laser beams, projected perpendicularly from the top of the room. Laser beams cross each other and they can be dynamically switched to new trajectories. The electronic control unit mounted on the top of the autonomous mobile platform then follows the current lit line and evaluates actions for the motor drives. Control system also includes collision detection with other mobile platforms or accidentally occurring objects.

articleTitle: H2 Norm Principle in Order Reduction of Discrete-time Systems
abstract: Numerical algorithms based on linear matrix in-equalities is presented for model order reduction of stable discrete-time linear systems using H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> norm principle. The set of policies is formulated to obtain matrix parameters of the state-space representation of the reduced-order discrete-time system. It is reiterated that the minimization of H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> norm of the approximation error leads to satisfactory approximation. The results and proposed regularization are listed to illustrate the validity of the method.

articleTitle: Application of evolutionary algorithms to analysis the possibilities of wind energy use
abstract: This publication presents the application of computer-aided analysis of the possibilities of potential using of wind energy. Correlation coefficients and an evolutionary algorithm method were discussed. An evolutionary method was used to analyze the amount of wind energy changes due to variation in weather conditions. Wind speed, cloud cover and chosen environmental conditions were measured over a period of several months. The correlation and the evolutionary algorithm analysis were performed. The amount of possible to gain wind energy related to the changes in weather conditions were calculated. According to the correlation coefficients and evolutionary algorithms wind speed during the year has no more than average correlation with air pollution in place of analyses. The Matlab / Simulink software was used for calculations.

articleTitle: System Optimization or Competition of Providers in Emergency Service System Reengineering
abstract: This paper deals with the emergency system reengineering, which consists in changing current positions of some centers operated by service providers. The reengineering can be performed in two different ways. In the first case a system administrator changes the locations of system service centers so that to minimize disutility perceived by an average system user respecting some rules, which protect a service providers from big changes of their sets of service centers. In the second case we consider more service providers competing for the profit under some rules imposed by the system administrator to protect system users from increase of perceived disutility. We assume that profit of a provider is proportional to transportation performance necessary to satisfy the demands of system users. In the first case, the administrator solution is obtained by solving the system reengineering problem using linear programming tools. The second case is modelled by Stackelberg's game and solved by an approximate solving technique for a game played by a leading service provider and the follower, which represents the other mutually cooperating providers. The both cases have been solved for a set of benchmarks and compared from the point of users and providers.

articleTitle: Coolant Injection System for Aircraft Engine Compressor
abstract: This paper studies a system of coolant injection into the compressor of an aircraft turbo-engine, used for its temporarily thrust augmentation, considered as a controlled object. The author has identified system's architecture and, based on it, has established system's motion equations, as its non-linear mathematical model; in order to linearize it, one has used the finite differences method and, after appropriate amplifying, one has transformed it into a dimensionless system; consequently, new forms for its equations and for their coefficients were established. The Laplace transformation applying brought the system to a usable form and, based on it, the block diagram with transfer functions was built. A study concerning system's stability was performed, as well as a study concerning its quality (system's step response) and some conclusions were presented, regarding system's pre-design and its using possibilities.

articleTitle: A Less Conservative Condition for Flexible Control Lyapunov Functions used in Networked Predictive Control Systems
abstract: Nowadays, the networked control systems (NCSs) are used in different industries, including the manufacturing plants, automotive systems, power production and distribution, tele-robotics and tele-medicine. The NCSs bring a lot of advantages when dealing with large plants, but they also come with disadvantages issued by the network-enhanced complexities, one of them being caused by data-packet dropouts. The disadvantages usually degrade the control systems performances and can even lead to instability. Thus, in this paper, the problem of compensating the negative effects induced by the data-packet dropouts is tackled. For this, a predictive controller with inherited input-to-state stability and robustness is designed; the controller is based on the so-called flexible control Lyapunov functions and makes use of a newly developed method to model the network-induced data-packet dropouts effect as a disturbance. The flexibility of the control Lyapunov function is constrained by means of a new less conservative solution. The method's efficiency was tested in simulation on an electric power-assisted steering system controlled through controller area network and the results are promising.

articleTitle: Fault Detection Using Consensus-Based Linear Distributed Kalman Filtering
abstract: The paper addresses the discrete-time distributed Kalman filtering over a sensor network to generate system fault residuals. The problem of interest are distributed sensor data consensus filtering for systems whose dynamics, as well as the control objectives, are not decoupled. Limited to linear systems and fixed network connectivity, the state observability and fault detectability is analyzed to guarantee stability of the distributed filters and responsibility of fault residuals. The performance of fault residuals generated within distributed Kalman filtering algorithms are demonstrated in the numerical example.

articleTitle: Cooperative traffic control based on greenhouse gases footprint minimization
abstract: Traffic control in major cities has consumed a lot of research efforts in the last years. Due to the increasing number of cars, the time spent in traffic can be significant. A large number of methods for reducing traffic jams were carried out, almost all by optimizing the traffic depending on the minimization of some metrics related exclusively to the traffic features (car numbers, speed of travel, distance, etc.). Unfortunately, very few cars have electric motors yet. So, one of the most dramatic effect of the traffic is the pollution, especially with greenhouse effect gases. The traffic control algorithms usually don't take into account this effect, so they can lead to greenhouse gases accumulation in some areas when traffic is redirected by these algorithms. In a previous paper we have presented the idea of using low energy small devices able to measure some greenhouse gases concentration for determining the pollution in some specific areas. These devices can connect via Bluetooth with mobile phones and can communicate the pollution levels. Thus, the pollution levels can be used as additional constraints in traffic control algorithms. In this paper we present a solution based on microcontroller devices which measures the greenhouse gases and act as agents. If the concentration of greenhouse gases increases, the devices can negotiate the penalization of the route depending on the destination, travel time, etc. Also, they can send the negotiation results to a central server, which can estimate if the accepted solution will generate further increases of gases concentration over an accepted level in other locations.
